## d856: slight, weak, contemptible

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d856 |
| Comparative input | *eḷ-i; *iḷ-a; strong *eḷḷ |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | e/i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ḷ / singleton/strong by formation |
| Following vowel | i/a/u |
| Root/formation shape | VC-i / VC-a / VCC |
| Grammatical category | adjective/verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | High-i, low-a and strong formations are independently attested. |
| Input class | short-strong-or-mixed-structure |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high root; medium exact Telugu formation |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil eḷi/eḷimai and Malayalam eḷi/eḷima establish high-i singleton formation, alongside independently low-a iḷamai/iḷama and strong eḷḷu.

**Direction.** Southern forms and historical Kannada iḷi agree on vowel-first order. Telugu ellidamu retains the vowel and a strengthened lateral; the strengthening is a local or borrowed formation, not evidence of universal original gemination.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *eḷ-i > eḷi/iḷi retains order; *eḷḷ > Tamil eḷḷu and Telugu ellidamu-like strength has a separate history. Tamil eṇmai follows l/n assimilation in a nominal suffix environment.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Telugu is a retained-order observation but exact input strength and inheritance of ellidamu are uncertain. Do not classify all weak/light words as geminate merely from Telugu. Possible relation to young513 and poor911 or contempt776 is semantic/derivational and must be tested, not used to manufacture one regular class.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR856

<a id="d857"></a>
## d857: bear

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d857 |
| Comparative input | *eḷ-V-ñc; regional *uḷ-iy-am and *el-uK |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | e/i/u / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ḷ/l / singleton |
| Following vowel | unknown/i/u |
| Root/formation shape | VC-V-NC / VC-uK / VC-iy-am |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Different animal-name extensions and paradigms remain distinct. |
| Input class | short-vowel-initial-singleton-apical |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for order; medium for full root |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil iḷai/uḷiyam/elu, Malayalam uḷiyam, Parji ili and Gondi eṛj establish vowel-first lateral/apical forms with several extensions. Konda olzu/oṛzu independently supports apical before z.

**Direction.** The distribution supports an earlier vowel preceding the apical; the displayed alternative *joḷǯ- is a separate reconstruction and cannot override the comparative onset evidence without an initial-y account.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *eḷ-Vñc > Gondi eṛj and Konda olzu/oṛzu involves syncope and palatal/nasal changes while retaining vowel-first order. Kui oli/oḍi and Kuvi oṛi reflect apical merger/stop development. Tamil eṇku and Malto eju have medial cluster reductions. Telugu elūgu is unusual in its long second vowel and needs separate suffix history.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** No positive initial displacement is attested despite several eastern languages. Exact ancestral vowel/formative varies and is not inferred from modern outcomes. Konda north/west rhotic versus south/east lateral is useful dialect correspondence, not necessarily metathesis variation. Animal-name diffusion remains possible but does not explain away the retained forms.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR857; K03 reconstruction *eḷ-V-ñc

<a id="d859"></a>
## d859: throw, strike, shoot

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d859 |
| Comparative input | *e/iṟ-i/u; long *ēṟ; labial extensions |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | e/i / short/long by formation |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/u/a |
| Root/formation shape | VC-i / VC-C / VVC |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Short labial verb and independent long noun differentiated; no suffix recovered solely from output. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high root order; low exact Telugu mm suffix |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil eṟi/iṟu, Malayalam eṟiyuka, Kannada iṟi and Konda iṟ independently establish vowel-first alveolar order. Long ēṟu/ēṭu blow is independently attested and not shortened to fit the short branch.

**Direction.** Broad southern and Konda/Kuvi vowel-first reflexes precede Telugu ṟimmu and Gondi rē/rēh under a displacement account. Exact labial formative of ṟimmu is less certain than root order.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *iṟ-(V)mm > *ṟimm gives Telugu ṟimmu if that strong labial derivative is established; a high-vowel root is independent, but mm must not be invented from the outcome. Gondi rē/rēh likely displaces a vowel-first stem while other dialects retain ērīstānā/ertānā. Kannada ṟeppu is an initial-loss/displaced-looking labial form with unexplained e. Kui ig-b > ibg is separately supported local cluster exchange.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Quantity and suffix predictions remain conditional: independent iṟi does not establish the exact mm derivative. Kannada initial ṟeppu may be local development or contact, not a family-wide exceptionless process. Kui ig root versus ṟ needs an allomorphic/correspondence explanation, while Kuvi ir remains unchanged. Toda mediative-causative eṯ is morphologically distinct from the throwing root and not an independent ordinary verb vote.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR859

<a id="d860"></a>
## d860: pull, drag, pluck

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d860 |
| Comparative input | regional *ṟel / *er-i / *ar-i; deeper order uncertain |
| Initial consonant | Ø/r |
| V1 quality / quantity | e/a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r/ṟ/l / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | VC-i versus CVC |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Final-l and labial derivatives require independent reconstruction. |
| Input class | uncertain-initial-order |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | low for common full input |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | lookalike-unresolved |

**Independent input evidence.** Gondi ari/eri full forms coexist with Konda ṟel, Kui jel and Pengo jel. Telugu remmu has a labial formation, not the same medial/final consonants as all the eastern stems.

**Direction.** Gondi may preserve an earlier vowel-first root, but the broad regional ṟel/jel series and its final l cannot be derived by a bare reversal of ari. The displayed *Rel is a regional reconstruction, not independently settled deeper order.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A conditional *eṟ-Vl > *ṟel could account for the Konda/Kui/Pengo series, with later ṟ>j, but no full identical -Vl formation is attested here. Telugu *eṟ-(V)mm > remmu requires a different derivative. Alternatively the Gondi ari material and eastern ṟel stems are distinct or only distantly related.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep the entire displacement claim uncertain rather than inventing *erel/*erimm to explain each result. Needed: older Gondi/Konda paradigms, independent final-l derivative, and regular correspondences linking Telugu mm to the same root. The several Gondi bringing/taking compounds do not add independent lexical votes.

**Mechanism scope.** Competing cognacy and displacement hypotheses.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR860; DEN1 1972 p.415 entry4243

<a id="d865"></a>
## d865: red

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d865 |
| Comparative input | *eṯ-V; *eṯ-a/*eṯ-up |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ/ṯ / singleton and strengthened formations |
| Following vowel | a/u |
| Root/formation shape | VC-a / VC-uP; strengthened VCC-a |
| Grammatical category | adjective/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Low-a adjective and -up noun independently distinguished. |
| Input class | short-strong-or-mixed-structure |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high regional order; medium deeper cognacy |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Konda eṟa/eṟani and Tamil eṟuṛ̆am red-flowered tree independently support short initial e before an alveolar; Telugu eṟupa and historical Eṟama have singleton evidence beside modern eṟṟa.

**Direction.** The independent Konda form and singleton variants favor a vowel-first root, not a primitive initial r. Gemination in Telugu is not uniformly ancestral.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *eṯ-a > eṟa and strengthened eṟṟa retain initial order; *eṯ-up > eṟupa has a different noun expansion. Gondi erra is explicitly borrowed from Telugu and must not become an independent inherited retention.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The source dates Eṟama as an eighth-century name and Eṟṟana as the fourteenth-century author; these are lexicographic date claims pending inscription verification. Tamil botanical semantic link is less direct than Konda colour, and Kolami eroṛi/erroḍī may be regional loans. Possible relationship to red/dog817 and clay820 requires a cognacy argument, not automatic merging of colour roots.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR865; K03 regional *eṯ-V

<a id="d868"></a>
## d868: say, quotative; literary contracted grammatical forms

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d868 |
| Comparative input | regional *an/en/in; proposed deeper *aHn; grammatical *an-an, *an-ā-baḍu etc. |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | a/e/i / short regional roots; long northern grade and grammatical contractions |
| C2 identity / structure | n / nasal with tense-conditioned cluster variants |
| Following vowel | a/ā/u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | VC+infinitive/passive/negative morphology |
| Grammatical category | verb/quotative |
| Boundary evidence | Full and reduced infinitive, passive, post-action and negative paradigms explicitly paired in source. |
| Input class | nasal-quotative-morphology |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for local an+suffix order; medium for phonetic mechanism |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | nasal-grammatical-displacement |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil eṉ, Kannada an/ennu, Tulu anpini/inpini and Telugu anu independently establish vowel before n; Old Telugu envānṟu preserves an e variant. K03 proposed *aHn explains wider vowel alternation but is not needed to establish local segment order.

**Direction.** Sastri1969 p.72 explicitly aligns full anu derivatives with literary n-initial variants, independently of the modern base alone. Kota in:n also shows initial-vowel absence but need not share the Telugu mechanism.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Telugu *an-an > nān and *an-ā-baḍu > nābaḍu can involve displacement/contraction; negative *an-aka > nāka requires merger/loss of one a. The source also gives anaru:naru with short a, so one unqualified long-output rule does not cover the whole paradigm. Analogical stem extension and phonological reduction compete; passage-by-passage morphology is needed.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** These are literary grammatical formations, not evidence that ordinary nasal roots joined the classical nonnasal apical rule. Nasal augmentation in negayu<egayu and nuṇḍi<uṇḍi is a different process. Tamil/central tense alternants n:nt/t/c/s reflect inherited morphology and assimilation, not initial movement. Kota n could be simple aphaeresis. Kurux long ā and the deep laryngeal reconstruction remain separate vowel-history questions. No exact date of the individual literary forms is established by Sastri’s period label.

**Mechanism scope.** Literary grammatical nasal displacement/contraction or analogical allomorphy; distinct from the classical nonnasal apical domain.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR868; Sastri1969 p.72 visually checked; K03 comparative reconstruction records

<a id="d869"></a>
## d869: sunshine, dry in sun

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d869 |
| Comparative input | *en-ṯ-V / *enṯ |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | nṯ / nasal-stop cluster |
| Following vowel | u/a |
| Root/formation shape | VNC-V |
| Grammatical category | noun/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Nasal cluster independently reconstructed; derived dry/grain forms nested. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for cluster |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | root-cluster-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil eṉṟu and Telugu eṇḍa/eṇḍu independently establish a nasal-apical cluster. Gondi eddi/addī and Naiki edde can reflect medial assimilation of that cluster.

**Direction.** Nasal and apical follow the initial vowel in the independent southern witnesses. Parji nendi/nenḍi adds an initial nasal whose origin cannot simply be called initial apical displacement.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *enṯ > eṉṟ/eṇḍ retains cluster order; *enṯ > edd is assimilation and possible denasalization. Parji nendi could reflect nasal prothesis, analogy with day words or a different extension; the medial nasal remains, so simple swapping of the sole n is inadequate.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A root-cluster control, not an exception invented from its retained result. Toda eṟ in a song is explicitly labeled probably spurious by the newer dictionary, so it contributes no secure singleton evidence. Connection to el shine829 or eṟi861 is a lexical hypothesis; no automatic collapse until the lateral/nasal/stop derivation is supported.

**Mechanism scope.** Cluster retention/assimilation; Parji prothesis/analogy unresolved.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR869; Toda2025 p.15 entry20 explicitly doubtful

<a id="d910"></a>
## d910: seven, seventy

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d910 |
| Comparative input | short *eẓ-u-pat- tens versus long *ēẓ-u numeral |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | e / mixed by formation |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | VC-u + ten / VVC-u |
| Grammatical category | numeral |
| Boundary evidence | Short attributive/tens grade and long independent numeral are independently attested in several languages. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam eẓu-patu seventy and short attributive eẓu- independently establish the short root beside ēẓu seven. Tulu eḷpa and Kodagu əḷu-vadɨ independently retain a short tens formation.

**Direction.** Southern short attributive/tens forms support e before ẓ. Telugu ḍebbadi promotes the apical, whereas ēḍu preserves the independent long root in numeral and person formation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *eẓ-(u)-pat > *ẓe-ppat > ḍebbadi is schematic: vowel loss, displacement, labial strengthening/voicing and the Telugu tens suffix require separate chronology. Later ḍebbʰai/ḍabbʰai adds suffix contraction, aspiration and e/a variation. Long *ēẓ-u > ēḍu retains order; no ad hoc shortening of modern ēḍu is required to feed seventy.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The compound boundary supplies independent conditioning information, but exact prehistoric weakening of u and voicing of p cannot be inferred merely from a compound label. The original ḍ in seventy remains distinct from later d elsewhere; orthography/source traditions need checking before claiming one universal merger date. K03 p.264 diagnoses Kolami seven forms as Telugu loans. Kui oḍgi is itself queried and has separate vowel/suffix history, not initial metathesis.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 p.264 §6.5.7; PSS83 p.235; DEDR 910

## d913: song, metre; sing

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada ēḷe and Telugu ēla independently agree in long ē before lateral. Malto éle marks stress, not independently long quantity.

**Direction.** Both southern forms and Malto keep vowel-before-lateral order; no need to privilege Telugu.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *ēḷ-V > Kannada ēḷe and Telugu ēla, with lateral correspondence and final vowel differing. Malto él-e may support the root but does not establish a long proto-vowel by itself.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A regional song/metre name may diffuse; Kannada–Telugu agreement alone does not rule out borrowing. The Malto singing comparison is semantically compatible but sparsely attested. Keep the family as a qualified long-input retention control, not a metathesis case.

<a id="d915"></a>
## d915: separate, winnow, sift

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d915 |
| Comparative input | *ēṟ- / shorter extended *eṟ-l-; possible *cēṟ connection |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | ē/e / long and independently short extended forms |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/i/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | VVC-C / VC-l-is |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for mixed quantity; low for immediate displaced input |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | long-short-formation-challenge |

**Independent input evidence.** Telugu ēṟu and widespread Gondi ēri/ēr, Konda ēṟ and Kui/Kuvi ē- establish long vowel-first formations. Konda eṟlis and Kuvi erl independently supply shorter extended formations, but not the complete prehistory of ṟēs/jēc.

**Direction.** Widespread vowel-first order versus Konda ṟēs and Pengo jēc supports displacement-family comparison. It does not establish long ē as the immediate input of those precise derivatives, given the independently present short eṟl formation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Retained *ēṟ-s/p gives Gondi ērst-, Kuvi ērs/ērsp/ēhp and Konda ēṟp. Konda ṟēs and Pengo jēc could reflect long-input displacement or a lost short extended *eṟ-V-s/c; the latter is not directly attested. Kui ēspa/ēja and Kuvi ēhp show consonant developments without initial displacement. Konda nēspa requires additional prothesis or morphological history, not movement of an inherited initial n from this root.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A genuine quantity challenge remains: do not classify ṟēs/jēc as verified short-input outcomes because their outputs are long. Conversely, the full set is not proof that all long roots were eligible. Malayalam ekaṟuka has extra k and cannot simply be treated as the identical unextended stem. DEDR queries relation to cēṟ/cēṭṭai2019; initial c loss, cognacy and formation must be argued separately. Konda nēspa is preserved as an unresolved variant; it could show secondary n as in other Telugu-region verbs, but no source diagnosis is asserted.

**Mechanism scope.** Displacement-family comparison; direct long exchange versus unattested short derivative unresolved.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR915 p.88; DEDR source cross-reference2019

<a id="d916"></a>
## d916: rise, ascend, rouse; dawn; water-lift

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d916 |
| Comparative input | *ēṟ / *ēl; displaced regional rē/lē derivatives; alternative *sal? |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | ē / long independently attested; immediate displaced input unresolved |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ/l / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | VVC / VVC-V; disputed earlier short derivatives |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Different rise, dawn, imperative and water-lift formations; no unverified short grade treated as established. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for comparative long root; low for immediate displaced derivative |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | long-input-challenge |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil ēṟu/ēl, Malayalam ēṟuka/ēlkka, Kannada ēṟu, Kota ēṯ/ēr and Toda long-apical forms independently establish long root quantity and vowel-before-apical order. No independently full short *er-V derivative matching Telugu rēgu/lēcu is supplied by the present set.

**Direction.** Widespread southern long V-apical order contrasts with Telugu rē-/lē- in the same broad rise/rouse meanings. This supports displacement-family comparison, but does not by itself prove that a long vowel was the immediate input: an independently documented earlier short grade or different root would change that conclusion.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A direct *ēṟ > rē or *ēl > lē reverses a long vowel and apical, outside the short-input rule. Alternatively an earlier short extended *er/el-V could yield the long displaced forms, but that intermediate is currently unsupported. Telugu reccu needs its own shortening/strong derivative history. Water-lift ētamu preserves V-apical order after strong dental development. Konda ēṟasi versus defective le/leˀ e/ledu shows formation/morphological contrast, not a simple dated sound-change sequence.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep this as a genuine challenge in the long-input class, with immediate prehistory uncertain, rather than silently moving it to short input. The alternative *sal? reconstruction is connected to Brahui saling and requires a separate initial-s and vowel history; Brahui alone does not demonstrate a common *sal that explains every southern form. The unrelated *ñāl dog head is a database linkage error. Kannada rēgu and Tulu rēgiyuni could be shared regional developments or Telugu loans; no donor proof is available here. Central les/lēp also requires contact evaluation. Gondi cooking forms and Kuvi re'nai are explicitly questioned in DEDR; the Kuvi source disagrees ascend versus descend. Relation to short *eẓ rise851 could involve conflation or analogy but is not assumed; ẓ versus ṟ/l needs independent justification.

**Mechanism scope.** Displacement-family comparison supported; direct long-vowel metathesis versus lost short grade or etymological conflation unresolved.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR916 p.88 directly read; contrast DEDR851 p.82

## d917: male buffalo, bull, male animal

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d917 |
| Comparative input | *ēṯ / *ēṟ- |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | ē / long |
| C2 identity / structure | ṯ/ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/u/an |
| Root/formation shape | VVC / VVC-V |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | long-apical-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for southern long order |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | long-input-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil ēṟu/ēṟṟai, Malayalam ēṟu/ēṟan and Kota/Toda ēṟ establish long ē before apical. Strong Tamil ṟṟ/ṭṭ supports an alveolar/dental-stop reconstruction rather than treating every r as primary rhotic.

**Direction.** Several independent southern branches have the same vowel-first order; Brahui arē also retains a vowel before r but has its own vocalism.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *ēṯ-u > Tamil ēṟu, Malayalam ēṟu and southern ēṟ; reinforced ēṟṟai/ēṭṭai. Brahui arē/arisk could involve suffixation and vowel redistribution but does not show root-apical promotion to word onset.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Kota tirēr/tir e·r is a compound, not a doubled metathesis result. Brahui arē comparison requires explicit vowel and plural analysis; do not count final ē as proof of a swap because r remains preceded by a. Badaga ēgaru has extra g and an alternative calf cross-reference, so its cognacy is less secure than ēru. DEDR questions connection with sēṟi2820; initial-s history remains outside this control.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR917 p.88; Krishnamurti reconstruction in database

## d931: carry in loads, cart

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d931 |
| Comparative input | *ok-; transitive *ok-p- |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | k / nonapical velar |
| Following vowel | zero |
| Root/formation shape | VC-p |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Independent root ok plus transitive p, contrasted with past t. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for velar-labial order |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | nonapical-kp-domain |

**Independent input evidence.** Konda and Pengo ok-, Parji okp:okt and Kui past okt establish velar before labial in the transitive stem independently of the Kui present opka.

**Direction.** The base ok and retained Parji okp directly support k-p as earlier than Kui p-k. This is not an apical input.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *ok-p-a > opka in Kui, while past *ok-t yields okt. Parji preserves okp:okt; Konda okis is a different causative formative. Pengo bare ok supplies a root control, not the same -p formation.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The red *kem head is a database linkage error and is excluded. Gadaba oskap has additional s and cannot independently establish a simple identical stem. Gondi akanā may reflect vowel lowering or different formation/cognacy. The source compares Tamil oy984, but the relationship k:y needs separate reconstruction. This supplies one additional Kui k-p formation, not a Telugu metathesis case.

**Mechanism scope.** Consonant-cluster k-p > p-k, separate from initial apical displacement.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR931 p.90 directly read

<a id="d945"></a>
## d945: with, together; agree, reconcile

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d945 |
| Comparative input | *uṭ-an / *oṭ-an; compound *oṭam#paṭ- |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short base with long grammatical variants |
| C2 identity / structure | ṭ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | VC-a-n # verb; grammatical suffix variants |
| Grammatical category | postposition/adverb/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Independently matching comitative plus paṭ/baḍ compound; n>m before labial. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for full compound |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | compound-aphaeresis-comparison |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil uṭaṉ and uṭam-paṭu, Malayalam uṭan/uṭam-peṭuka and Kannada oḍan/oḍam-baḍu independently establish a full comitative base and compound boundary.

**Direction.** The matching full compound in several southern languages supports initial-vowel loss in Tulu dambaḍ-; Telugu also preserves the full compound, but is not the sole order witness.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oḍam#baḍ- > Tulu oḍam-baḍipuni beside dambaḍipuni by aphaeresis plus retroflex simplification; medial a remains and no output long vowel is required. Telugu oḍam/oḍã-baḍu has nasalization/loss at the boundary without initial apical movement. Grammatical -oṭu/-ōṭu and Toda -vɨṛ require their own clitic/prosodic history.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Tulu initial d is therefore not automatic evidence for the Telugu contraction process. Loss of initial o alone plus ḍ>d accounts for the observed segment sequence; a literal exchange would additionally need vowel fusion/loss and offers no independent advantage here. Badaga ōṭalu hotel with a following postposition gloss is a parser conflation, not a cognate comitative word. Morphological compounds and suffix allomorphs are not independent roots.

**Mechanism scope.** Tulu aphaeresis and stop simplification; no unique evidence for literal vowel-apical exchange.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR945 p.90 directly read

## d946: break, burst; crack; defeat

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d946 |
| Comparative input | *oṭ-i / *oṭ-ay; long *ōṭ variants |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | o/u / short and independently long formations |
| C2 identity / structure | ṭ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/ay |
| Root/formation shape | VC-V; long and strong nominal formations |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for comparative short and long forms |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | mixed-quantity-formation-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil oṭi/uṭai, Malayalam oṭiyuka/uṭayuka and Kannada oḍi establish short retroflex roots with distinct i/ay formations; long hole/burst forms recur independently in SD I, CD and eastern languages.

**Direction.** Numerous vowel-first roots across branches support original V-ṭ. Long Telugu ōḍu is not evidence that a short metathesized stage occurred because the apical remains after the vowel.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Short *oṭ-i/ay yields oḍi/oḍe and related strong derivatives; separately long ōṭ/ōḍ produces ōr/ōh/ōj in eastern languages. Toda vaṛ and Gondi vōṛ have initial glide development, while r/ṛ remains postvocalic. Tamil noṭi has secondary n, not root-apical promotion.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Telugu defeat forms are explicitly questioned against run-away1041; retain them as uncertain cognacy, not extra exceptions. Gondi urung/oruŋ may instead belong with snap662, and the database ruŋ is only that cross-reference, not an attested Gondi displacement in946. Original source separates Kodagu oḍe/oḍa paradigms that the database misassigns Kannada. Kui ohpa length is queried in DEDR; keep short source and proposed ōhpa distinct. No deterministic reconstruction of every long form from the short root has been established.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR946 p.91 directly read; alternative1041/662

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil oṭu, Malayalam oṭuvu and Kannada oḍise/oḍucu supply full short vowel-first forms with independently variable high suffixes.

**Direction.** Vowel-first forms across several southern branches establish input order; Telugu vaḍise cannot override them.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oṭ-is > oḍise; Telugu oḍise-gaḍḍa : vaḍise-gaḍḍa shows initial glide/vowel development (o > va or related prothetic history), with the retroflex still after the first vowel. It is not *oḍ > ḍo.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Exact origin of va is unresolved without dialect/historical evidence; it may parallel rounded-vowel breaking elsewhere but that is not asserted as a dated Telugu rule. Both forms are one compound family, and the lump element gaḍḍa is not an extra root reflex.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d954: shrink, subdue, cease, leave

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d954 |
| Comparative input | *oṭ-uŋ / *oṭ-ukk; regional *uṭ-uŋ/uk |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | o/u / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṭ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u |
| Root/formation shape | VC-u-NC / VC-u-CC |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | short-vowel-initial-singleton-apical |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for order and u-formative; medium for immediate root-vowel quality |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core-vowel-history-variable |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil oṭuŋku/oṭukku, Malayalam oṭuŋŋuka/oṭukkuka, Kannada uḍugu/uḍagu and Kurux oṛᵒgnā establish vowel-first retroflex and nasal/strong formations. High u is independently present, though Kannada also has a.

**Direction.** SD I and North Dravidian full forms establish V-ṭ before Telugu/ Kui initial ḍ. This does not establish a unique o versus u at every regional stage.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *uṭ-uŋ > *ḍuuŋ > ḍūŋ with subsequent shortening before ŋk yields Telugu ḍuŋku; *oṭ-uŋ may instead yield short ḍoŋku directly under the different-vowel account. Long dō̃ku preserves another quantity/nasal variant. Kui ḍūmba/ḍūppa requires a labial formative distinct from Telugu velar; high u can support long u+u contraction if the prior regional root was u. No single intermediate is proven across all formations.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Telugu uḍugu/uḍuvu retain the original order in quit/cease meanings; semantic/formative differentiation is real but not yet a deterministic phonological rule. uḍupu may belong to1009, and Kolami ūḍp/ūrp is explicitly queried. Badaga okku may reflect medial assimilation rather than concealed metathesis. A connection to compressed aṭ roots63/80 or oṭṭ960 requires independent vowel and semantic history, not an automatic merge.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR954 p.91 directly read; contrast1009/960

## d958: adhere, join, heap; smear

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d958 |
| Comparative input | *oṭṭ- / *oṇṭ-; Central *oṭ-p- |
| Initial consonant | Ø |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil oṭṭu/oṇṭu, Malayalam oṭṭuka and Kannada oṭṭu/oḍḍu independently establish strong/geminate or nasal-cluster formations; a singleton dictionary head does not override them.

**Direction.** Vowel-first forms in SD I, Telugu and CD establish order; the independently strong SD I consonants explain why this is not a plain singleton-apical control.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oṭṭ > oṭṭu/oḍḍu with strength/voicing variation; Central oṭ-p/ or-p keeps vowel before apical plus labial. Kota oṭ/oc paradigms reflect local consonant developments, not initial displacement.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Smear and adhere meanings could connect separate strong formations; exact common reconstruction needs caution. Telugu fire-placing and total senses are not two roots for frequency counts. Relation to oath959 and place962 is semantically possible through bind/place but not automatic.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d959 |
| Comparative input | regional *oṭṭ/oḍḍ; Indo-Aryan *hōḍḍa comparison |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṭ / geminate independently supported |
| Following vowel | u/a |
| Root/formation shape | VCC-V |
| Grammatical category | noun/verb |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | short-strong-or-mixed-structure |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for strong regional form; inherited distribution uncertain |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | strong-cluster-contact-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil oṭṭu, Malayalam oṭṭam and Kannada oṭṭu/oḍḍu establish a strong medial stop independently of Telugu. Eastern singletons may reflect simplification or borrowing.

**Direction.** All selected forms keep vowel before the stop; the source does not require initial-stop metathesis.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oṭṭ > Telugu oṭṭu oath and oḍḍu wager; Kui oḍa and Kuvi oṭu/ottinai show regional strength variation. Kuvi ōtali has lengthening with vowel first, not a metathesis long-vowel product.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Indo-Aryan hōḍḍa/hoḍḍa and modern hoṛ forms require contact analysis; their initial h is not evidence for a Dravidian word-initial apical. CDIAL explicitly labels Sinhala oṭṭu as Tamil loan, which is not an independent Dravidian vote. Shared origin with adhere958/place962 remains a family sensitivity question.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR959; CDIAL14175

## d962: place, offer, extend; set net or snare

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |

| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |

| Overall confidence | medium |

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada oḍḍu and Tulu oḍḍuni independently support a strong medial retroflex matching Telugu oḍḍu. Old Telugu oḍuku is a distinct weaker extended form, not evidence that modern strength was original in every formation.

**Direction.** SD I and Telugu retain initial vowel; Gondi urrānā and Malto aḍye have the same order despite different consonant strength and vowel.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oḍḍ > oḍḍu and regional simplified oḍ; Old Telugu oḍuku requires derivational or strength-alternation history. No initial displacement is necessary.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Pali oḍḍeti set a net is explicitly compared; contact direction is not established here. Old Telugu inscription label has no date in this record, so it cannot anchor chronology. Do not merge place962 with bank965 or stake959 solely for phonetic identity; retain a documented sensitivity option.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR962; source Pali comparison

## d965: bank, shore, slope

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada oḍḍu/oṇḍi and Kurux oṭṭā independently support strong or nasal-cluster input, while Konda/Gondi/Kuvi singletons are daughter outcomes.

**Direction.** Cross-branch vowel-first forms and independent consonant strength support retained order, not reconstruction from Telugu alone.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oṭṭ-V > Telugu/Kannada oḍḍu, with simplification in Gondi/Konda/Kuvi oḍu. Nasal Kannada oṇḍi supplies a formation variant but does not uniquely prove common *oṇṭ.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Regional river terminology could diffuse, and the comparison does not prove every singleton is independently inherited. Badaga slope and numerous place names derive from one base; never count each name. Meaning could connect to a bank built by heaping958, but that semantic history is unproven.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Independent input evidence.** Kui oḍa and Kuvi odi/oditi/oḍ independently support short vowel-before-retroflex matching Telugu oḍikamu, but not its exact -ikam suffix.

**Direction.** The eastern full forms establish order independently of Telugu; all remain vowel first.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oṭ-i/V > odi/oḍa/oḍikamu; Kuvi oṭpi and oṭ show transitive/strong development while retaining vowel first. Light verbs in oṭpi ki are not pieces of a reconstructed root.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Beauty versus purity/recovery is a plausible semantic connection, with contact still possible in this regional set. Kui oṭka is stranded in the gloss and has not been newly normalized as an attestation. The high second vowel of Telugu matches Kuvi odi but the complete nominal derivation remains unestablished.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d985: slowly, gently; constantly

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada ollane/oyyane and Tamil oyy-eṉa establish a strong consonant and adverbial formation independently of Telugu ollana/oyyana.

**Direction.** All witnesses have vowel before lateral/glide; ll versus yy is a segmental alternation, not an order change.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *oll/oyy-an > ollane/ollana/oyyana, with Tamil eṉa quotative/adverbial material potentially separately grammaticalized. Kuvi olle olle is reduplicated.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Expressive origin, quotative material and ll/yy alternation prevent a unique singleton reconstruction. Kuvi constantly versus gently/slowly needs semantic caution and may reflect borrowing; Naikri regional diffusion also remains possible. Repeated olle is one adverbial formation.

<a id="d996"></a>
## d996: sound, cry, weep

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d996 |
| Comparative input | *ol-i/u; *ol-k; *ul-amp; long *ōl formations |
| Initial consonant | Ø |
| V1 quality / quantity | o/u / short root and separately long formations |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/u/zero/a |
| Root/formation shape | VC-V / VC-k / VC-a-mp; long nouns |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for northern ol-k comparison |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | mixed-formation-cluster-loss-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil oli/ulampu, Malayalam oli and Kannada uli independently support vowel-before-lateral. Kurux olx and Malto olg give an independently matching northern velar extension for comparison with Brahui hōɣ.

**Direction.** The northern full lateral-plus-velar forms are particularly strong evidence for order and for loss of lateral in Brahui; a Telugu metathesis model is unnecessary.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *ol-k > Kurux olx, Malto olg and, with lateral loss plus initial h/vowel history, Brahui hōɣ. Emeneau1997 pp.441–442 proposes this cluster-loss analysis and compares other lost preconsonantal laterals. Telugu uliyu/ulivu retains order; Tamil ōl/ōlam involves separate quantity formation. No root-lateral promotion is established.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Bray instead proposed imitative hō plus hiatus-bridging ɣ; Emeneau argues the comparative velar extension favors inheritance but leaves imperative/prohibitive ɣ absence unresolved. The source does not supply every intermediate explaining Brahui length and h. Keep that uncertainty visible; neither competing account is initial liquid metathesis. Tamil/Malayalam ulapp versus ulamp is nasal/strength variation. Potential relationship to strong oll expressives985 is not assumed.

**Mechanism scope.** Brahui cluster-member loss; competing imitative origin, not initial apical metathesis.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR996; Emeneau1997 pp.441–442 §§2.2–3 directly read; https://www.jstor.org/stable/619537

<a id="d1079"></a>
## d1079: vomit, regurgitate

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1079 |
| Comparative input | *kak; possible regional *kaẓ-k beside kak |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | k / possible ẓ / velar singleton/geminate; alternative apical+velar cluster |
| Following vowel | zero/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVC / possible CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Intensive -ba independently contrasts with kak; Telugu r history is a separate question. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for kak family; low for apical antiquity |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | input-uncertain-secondary-r-comparison |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kakku, Malayalam kakkuka, Gondi kakk/kokk, Konda kak and the Pengo/Manda kak bases independently support the nonapical root. Kannada kaṛ̆ku (=kaẓku) supplies a real apical-bearing variant beside kakku, so an apical input cannot simply be rejected because the headword is kak.

**Direction.** A regional *kaẓ-k could give Kannada kaẓku and Telugu krakku, but the many nonapical forms do not uniquely establish whether the apical is inherited, secondary or belongs to a different convergent formation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Two alternatives remain: (1) *kaẓ-k > *kẓak > krakku, with separate k strengthening, while other branches assimilate ẓk to kk; (2) inherited *kak > kakku, with secondary r in Telugu on the literary Cr pattern and a separately remodeled Kannada variant. Pengo kak + intensive-ba > kabga has a distinct velar–labial alternation, independently supported by its simple stem.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Telugu krakku is not counted as a secure classical displacement positive. Kannada kaẓku is the evidence that could favor that analysis, but its age and wider correspondences need checking. Cough/vomit vocabulary also permits expressive expansion. DEDR comparison1477 kāl is not accepted without independent semantic/phonological review. Badaga proper names and repeated God Šiva stories do not add lexical roots. The Kondh intensive and Telugu initial-r problem are separate processes in one family.

**Mechanism scope.** Ambiguous earlier apical versus secondary r in Telugu; separate Kondh morphological velar/labial alternation.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR1079; Garrett and Blevins2009 p.538 ex.20b; panel-030

## d1123: calf, young cattle

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1123 |
| Comparative input | *kaṭ-a-c / *kiṭ-a-v; regional apical+l formation |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a/i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṭ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-C |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |

| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | mixed-vowel-regional-apical |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kaṭavu/kaṭāri, Kannada kaḍasu and Kurux kaḍrū independently establish medial retroflex and full order; they do not establish one common ending for every cattle term.

**Direction.** Full southern and northern forms favor k-V-apical before Konda gṛālu and Kui grāḍu. Kota kēv has only a conjectured earlier cluster in DEDR.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kaṭ-al > *kṛāl > gṛālu and Kui grāḍu adds regional stop/rhotic and final-lateral changes; Kuvi ḍālu can follow C1 loss from a cluster. Telugu krēpu has unexplained ē/p under this comparison and alternatively belongs to1594.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep Telugu krēpu ambiguous in both entries, never two positive votes. Kui gāṛo retains postvocalic apical while ḍrāḍu alters C1; livestock age/sex labels and possible diffusion need separate lexical history. IA cattle comparanda are contact evidence, not extra Dravidian votes.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1123; current comparative cluster panel; DEDR alternative1594; no merged root asserted

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kaṇṇa supplies a geminate nasal, with no rhotic. Telugu kranna has an extra r rather than a clear one-for-one nasal reversal.

**Direction.** No comparison establishes a pre-Telugu kar/kaṟ input; Tamil is a possible cognate, not a warrant to delete r from its history.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible expressive kaṇṇa > kanna followed by secondary r yields kranna; alternatively a distinct rhotic root or false cognacy. kraccuṟa has additional affricate/rhotic material and cannot be generated by the same simple exchange.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Sparse adverbial comparison; literary expressive or analogical expansion is plausible but unproved. Need dated kanna/kranna variants or a fuller independently cognate r-bearing formation.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil karu/karuku, Kannada karaku/karñ-type formations and Gondi kar support short kar independently, beside widespread long kār. Exact Telugu -aŋ formation is not supplied by bare karu.

**Direction.** Full kar order across branches favors displacement in Telugu krā̃gu and Kui krumu/grīpa; their vowel differences require distinct formation histories.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kar-aŋ > *krāŋ > krā̃gu; kaggu/kaŋgu may follow lost r or direct medial assimilation. Kui *kar-um > krum could preserve the formative u by syncope/assimilation, whereas grīpa needs high-vowel formation or other quality change.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Long kāru is a separate retained formation, not proof every member had long input. Kui ī and Telugu inferred a remain unresolved. Kannada/Toda dark and charcoal derivatives contain internal assimilation/glide changes, not initial promotion. Personal/place names are not independent etyma.

## d1287: strong, abundant, excessive

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1287 |
| Comparative input | *kar-u; Telugu consonantal/nasal derivative |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V / CVC-ND |
| Grammatical category | adjective/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core-formation-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil karumai, Malayalam karu/karuttu and Kannada karu establish full kar order. Telugu karamu independently retains it.

**Direction.** Telugu krandu-konu promotes r before a relative to the full comparison; the exact nd derivative needs its own reconstruction.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kar-nd > *kra-nd > krandu-konu fits short consonantal displacement; *kar-a-nd followed by contraction/shortening is an alternative without independent exact suffix evidence.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Abundance and spreading senses can overlap neighboring kar families but do not establish merger. The light verb konu is not part of the original kar root. Kota numbness and Toda bush compounds have weak semantic alignment and are not counted as direct controls.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1287; current comparative cluster panel

## d1291: sound, call, ring

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1291 |
| Comparative input | *kar-ay; *kar-NK and labial formations |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-ay / CVC-NC |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil karai, Malayalam karayuka and Kannada kare independently support kar-a; Gondi karŋg supports consonantal/nasal formation without a full medial vowel.

**Direction.** Southern, Gondi and northern full roots favor k-a-r before Telugu krand/kraŋ and Kui krāv.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Consonantal *kar-ŋg > *kra-ŋg fits Telugu kraŋgu; krandu has a distinct dental nasal extension. Conditional *kar-av > krāv gives Kui bell tongue, but its exact suffix is not independently matched.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not count the bell noun and cry verb independently. Telugu short versus Kui long follows different formations; the contrast does not prove contraction followed by shortening in Telugu. Tulu gaggelyuni/Kota gagc can be expressive/internal assimilation, not concealed metathesis without evidence.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1291; current comparative cluster panel

## d1292: melt, dissolve

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1292 |
| Comparative input | *kar-a-NK; *kar-k; high-vowel derivatives |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/zero/i |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-NC / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada karaŋgu/karagu/kargu, Tamil karai and Telugu karãgu/karãcu independently provide full low and consonantal formations.

**Direction.** Cross-language full order plus within-Telugu retained forms favors innovation of krā̃gu/krā̃cu.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kar-aŋg > *kra-aŋg > *krāŋg > krā̃gu and stronger transitive *kar-aŋkk > krā̃cu are plausible; exact transitive consonant and palatalization chronology must be separately reconstructed. Kuvi karangali retains the full low formation.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A valuable low-formative positive with retained close controls: low a is not sufficient for obligatory application. Nasalized written forms do not by themselves date nasal loss. Neighboring Kannada/Telugu cognacy can involve old diffusion, but no source here establishes borrowing.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1292; current comparative cluster panel

## d1347: bonduc nut, molucca bean

**Independent input evidence.** Malayalam kaẓañci/kaẓacci and the composite Tamil kaẓaŋku/kaẓal/kaẓaṟci row supply full apical order; Tulu kaḷeñji supplies a lateral variant. The tuber headword is a semantic mislink.

**Direction.** Southern full ka-apical favors displacement in Telugu gracca, while gacca can follow r loss or direct medial assimilation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kaẓ-a-cc > *kẓācc > gracca requires shortening/strengthening; an earlier consonantal *kaẓ-cc > *kẓacc gives short a directly. The exact suffix and botanical transmission are not settled.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not import the kiẓ tuber reconstruction to explain this bonduc name. Kannada gajiga/gajjuga can be medial loss/palatalization without initial exchange; Tulu gajigɛ may be contact. Composite malformed Tamil row preserved as source evidence, not several independent records.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1347; current comparative cluster panel

## d1349: loosen, slip off; move, shake

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1349 |
| Comparative input | *kaẓ-al; *kaẓ-i; nasal-velar derivatives |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/i |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-l / CVC-i / CVC-NK |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |

| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada kaẓal and shorter kaẓi independently establish two apicals in the low-al formation.

**Direction.** Full kaẓ-al in several languages favors kẓā-l before Telugu krālu; final l is preserved rather than copied.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kaẓ-al > *kẓā-l > krālu. Gondi kaṛŋg retains initial order; Kui kṛeŋga/Pengo kṛaŋg are nasal-velar displaced formations with separate a/e development. Kui kṛepka additionally reverses stem-final k and suffix p.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Strongly supported segment order, but the Kui vowel cannot be read from the Telugu lateral suffix. The Sanskrit translation compound krālugaṇṭi uses the inherited verb; it does not make the root Sanskrit. Kota/Toda shortened strong forms allow medial assimilation without initial reordering.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1349; current comparative cluster panel

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil and Malayalam kaẓi independently establish full apical order; Telugu canal kayya/krayya is semantically narrower.

**Direction.** If canal is cognate with backwater, krayya promotes an older apical; final yy needs an extension or changed strong stem.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *kaẓ-y > *kẓa-y > krayya with strengthening; *kaẓ-iya with high-vowel loss is another route. kayya can follow r loss or direct ẓ/y assimilation.

**Direction.** Tamil full order and Kui medial apical make Telugu krammu/kraccu plausibly innovative.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kaẓ-m > *kẓam > krammu gives short vowel plus doubled labial; kraccu requires a different palatal formative. Syncope from *kaẓ-um before displacement is possible; final u is not automatically a contracting suffix.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The Tamil form supports the labial relationship but not exact geminate antiquity. Sparse distribution permits old contact, while no source establishes it. Kui garja is retained relative to the initial-order target despite separate affricate development.

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kāl/kāṟu, Kannada kāṟ and Kota/Kodagu long roots independently establish long quantity; Tulu karāya/karavɛ provide short-root expanded forms.

**Direction.** The full apical comparisons favor earlier k-V-apical before Telugu krāyu/grāyu, but do not establish one short contraction input.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *kar-āy > *krāy produces Telugu with aphaeresis/reassociation and suffixal long ā; alternatively *kār-y > krāy is long-vowel displacement. gāyu can then lose r, while initial k/g variation is separate.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A real quantity/formation residual outside a uniform short-root law. Tamil l/ṟ and nasal variants need comparative correspondence; neither is chosen merely to fit r. DEDR1079 kakku is an explicit comparison but not merged without a defensible apical/expressive history.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d1479: leg, foot, quarter

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1479 |
| Comparative input | *kāl |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā / long |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC free root |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Free root; compounds cannot supply a primitive CCr onset. |
| Input class | long-apical-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | long-free-root-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Gondi, Konda, Pengo and Manda independently attest kāl, establishing both long quantity and a free-root shape.

**Direction.** k precedes the long vowel and l follows it throughout the independently compared branches. Toda ō and Parji ē are local vowel reflexes, not transferred vowels.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kāl > Telugu kālu, Kui kāḍu, Kuvi kāl retains original order; Kui l>ḍ is compatible with the same change in displaced lateral roots but here occurs without displacement. Toda kōl and compound kōs̱ show vowel change and conditioned final fricativization. Tulu kārɯ has the lateral/rhotic correspondence.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The long free root is doubly outside the canonical short bound-root domain. Brahui trikkal is a compound whose initial tr belongs to the numeral material, not a reversal of kāl; inherited status and quantity of its kal member need separate contact investigation. Markodi short kar versus kār preserves source quantity variation, which cannot establish Proto-Dravidian short quantity. No independent bare-root metathesis is present.

**Mechanism scope.** Retention with vowel and lateral correspondences.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR1479; PSS83 p.229 (oldDED1238)

## d1507: Indian beech, Pongamia

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1507 |
| Comparative input | regional *kar-aŋ; tree compound *kar-aŋ#mar-an |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-NK |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |

| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |

**Independent input evidence.** Konda kaṛaŋ maran:kṛāŋ mrānu supplies a directly matching full versus clustered compound; Tulu korŋgi/korŋgu supplies retained r.

**Direction.** Both members of the Konda compound have independent full forms, establishing their order without privileging Telugu.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kar-aŋ > *krāŋ, with Telugu krānugu reflecting a further vowel/velar shape; later r loss gives kānugu/kānuga/kāngu. Tree maran>mrānu is d4711 and must not count as a second Pongamia-root event.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Botanical names can diffuse. Kannada kānagu has a different species identification (Dalbergia), so its semantic identity is uncertain. Exact Telugu medial -nu-gu versus Konda -ŋ needs nominal history; it is not supplied by a bare contraction.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1507; current comparative cluster panel; Separate tree-root d4711

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada kikkiṟi/kikkaṟisu and Telugu kikkiṟiyu independently agree on initial geminate k and later rhotic.

**Direction.** Telugu krikkiṟiyu has an additional initial r while retaining the later ṟ; literal movement of that sole rhotic is insufficient.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible kikkiṟiyu > krikkiṟiyu by secondary r or consonant-copying analogy; alternatively a reduplicative formation could have lost r in the full-looking forms. No independent older two-r form is established.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The compound kīkāraṇyamu contains Sanskrit araṇya and cannot reconstruct the simplex. DEDR compares1980 ceṟi and questions Sanskrit kiṣkindha; neither establishes a unique direction. Need dated variants or independent reduplicative morphology.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1509; current comparative cluster panel

<a id="d1574"></a>
## d1574: cry, crow, make noise

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1574 |
| Comparative input | *kil-a/ay; *kil-i and expressive extensions |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/i |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a / CVC-i / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Low-a crow and high/expressive shriek formations differentiated by independent southern morphology. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-other-apical |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil cilai, Malayalam cila/cilekka, Kannada kele and Tulu kele-puni independently support a low-a formation with initial k/c-V-l. Tamil cil and Gondi kil also supply a bare root; reduplicative shrieking stems have different morphology.

**Direction.** Southern and Gondi full forms support k-V-l before Kui kl-. Palatalization in Tamil and some Kannada/Telugu forms is a separate initial k development; none requires reconstructing initial c in the common input.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kil-a-p > *klēp > klāpa is the K80 lowering analysis; an alternative lowers/assimilates before cluster creation. Kui klīri and Kuvi klīrinai show a different high-vowel expressive formation, not an exception to low-a-specific lowering. Telugu kilārucu/kelayu/celãgu retains initial vowel/l order.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Postconsonantal l lies outside the narrow Telugu r/ṟ/ẓ metathesis set, while Kui admits it. This supports a structural language contrast, not simply a difference in frequency. Exact ancient morphology of the long ā Telugu expressive stem and klīri is not recoverable from the bare *kil head alone. Toda kīl ik is explicitly a Badaga loan; initial-loss Kota iḍ and alternative-cognacy jelk remain uncertain. Toda kv-style processes elsewhere must not be generalized to this root.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 pp.497–499 item 6; PSS83 p.230 post-C sonorant restriction; DEDR 1574

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada kaẓal and Tamil kiẓāaṉ independently supply a medial approximant and a following low vowel, with distinct final l/n.

**Direction.** The full cross-language forms favor earlier k-V-ẓ before Telugu krānu; kānu can subsequently lose r.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kaẓ-an > *kẓān > krānu > kānu preserves final n. Tamil ki and long ā plus Kannada final l show that this exact immediate form is reconstructed, not simply copied from one modern cognate.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Dairy vocabulary is geographically narrow and may diffuse. Vowel alternation and final n/l morphology remain unresolved; do not treat each differing ending as an independently confirmed contraction input.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada kiṟi/kiṟa/kiṟu and Tulu kiri/kiru independently establish the velar and short vowel; Tamil ciṟu reflects palatalization rather than an originally universal c.

**Direction.** The full southern root supports earlier ki-apical order before Telugu kriyyu. Telugu ciṟu retains full order and palatalizes; kriyyu can block that context after reordering.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kiṟ-y > *kṟiy > kriyyu, with strengthening of the formative, or high-vowel syncope before movement. krēpu calf has a separate low/long formation or belongs to1123, so it is not a secure positive here.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The database mouse compound *kiṯṯ-eli is not an ancestor of all small/young derivatives. Palatalization chronology is plausible but initial k preservation alone is insufficient because borrowing or expressive formations can also preserve k. Strong ṟṟ/tt variants are distinct formations.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d1595: whirl, be giddy, turn a mill

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kiṟukiṟu/kiṟukku, Kannada giṟi/giṟu/giṟa and Tulu giriyuni independently establish k-i-apical order and several formations.

**Direction.** The comparative full stems agree with retained Brahui kirrefing, not an initial kr- stem.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Intervocalic voicing and ṟ>r vary by language; expressive gemination gives giṟṟ-/girr- without initial displacement. Emeneau analyzes Brahui kirrefing as causative of hypothetical *kirreng, explicitly not an attested simplex.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is a k-initial retention control for the very small Brahui t/p-heavy sample. Its expressive geminates and several suffix vowels prevent treating every form as one identical singleton formation. Telugu gīra has secondary or separate quantity; Badaga kiri moguḍu funeral object is semantically uncertain. Marathi girakṇẽ is a contact comparison, not an independent inherited Dravidian vote.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

<a id="d1619"></a>
## d1619: below, lower, east

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1619 |
| Comparative input | short *kiẓ-nd / *kiẓ-V-kk versus long *kīẓ |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | i / mixed by formation |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-nd / CVC-V-kk / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | postposition/adjective/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Short/long grades independently attested; Telugu consonantal local formation not identical to southern east -kk. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam kiẓakku and Kannada kiẓ/kiẓgu independently establish a short allomorph alongside long kīẓ. Parji kiṛi corroborates short vowel before apical. K03 p.128 uses immediate *kiẓ-nd for Telugu below.

**Direction.** Southern short and long forms establish k-V-apical order. Telugu krinda places the apical before the vowel; kinda can be connected to it by independently attested cluster simplification.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kiẓ-nd > *kẓind > krind > kind gives krinda/kinda. Displacement removes the front vowel from immediately after k, blocking Telugu k>c palatalization; later r-loss restores ki after that palatalization has ceased to act on this item. Long kīḍupaḍu retains the apical medially; krī may be a separate contraction or abbreviated derivative.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is a relative chronology argument conditional on inheritance and the independently established palatalization environment, not proof from an isolated unpalatalized k. Do not shorten the citation root kīẓ ad hoc: a short allomorph is independently attested. Exact -nd and -nc history is less secure than initial order. Nilgiri/Brahui kī types admit medial-apical loss without displacement; they do not independently prove the Telugu route.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 p.128 Rule 14, p.158 Rule 21; DEDR 1619

## d1680: eyeball, egg, round object

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1680 |
| Comparative input | *kuṭ/guḍ; regional *gurḍ? |
| Initial consonant | k/g |
| V1 quality / quantity | u / short |

| Following vowel | u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC / CVCC |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |

| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |

**Independent input evidence.** Kannada guḍḍu and Tulu kuḍu establish a nonrhotic round-object stem. Konda gurḍu/gurzu supplies a real r-bearing comparison, unlike its explicitly Telugu-borrowed guḍu.

**Direction.** The extra r in Telugu gruḍḍu may correspond to Konda gurḍ, but the wider comparison does not uniquely establish its antiquity.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *gur-ḍ > gruḍḍu with strengthening; alternatively guḍḍu acquires literary r or interacts with blind1787, and Konda rhotic variants require their own source history. guḍḍu is not automatically evidence of later r loss.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Blind1787 has independent kuruḍu; egg does not share that reconstruction merely through homophony. Konda/Kuvi loan labels apply to guḍu, not automatically all rhotic variants. Earlier attestations of egg gruḍḍu/gurḍu would distinguish the alternatives.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1680; current comparative cluster panel

## d1767: bend, droop, sink low

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuraŋku and Kannada kurgu independently supply r and full/cluster formations; Kota koṛng also retains the medial apical.

**Direction.** Full cross-branch order favors Telugu kruŋgu and Kui krōŋga as displaced-family outcomes; Tamil kūr is a separate long grade.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Consonantal *kur-ŋg > kruŋgu; low-vowel *kur-aŋg > *kor-aŋg > krōŋga could yield Kui. Telugu kuŋgu could lose initial-cluster r or assimilate internally, as Kannada kuŋgu/kuggu does.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not impose one identical suffix vowel on both languages. Manda grūc adds long ū/palatal formation not explained by that o-a derivation. Alternative related sink1826 supplies only clusters and is tested in family-merge sensitivity.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d1769: monkey

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1769 |
| Comparative input | *kur-aŋk; regional *kor-a-nt? |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |

| Grammatical category | noun |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuraŋku, Malayalam kuraŋŋu, Kannada koraŋgi and Tulu kuraŋga independently establish a low-a nasal-velar noun.

**Direction.** The full r-bearing monkey name favors earlier k-V-r before Telugu krō̃ti; exact dental versus velar suffix correspondence remains a separate question.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kor-ant > *krōnt > krō̃ti > kō̃ti; this is not direct transformation of Tamil kuraŋku into Telugu. A velar-to-dental suffix history or distinct formative must be justified.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Tamil kōnti is explicitly Telugu borrowing. Kannada/Tulu kōti and central kōti may also diffuse, but absent explicit source evidence remain uncertain transmission cases, not automatic independent metatheses. Species and monkey-name replacement need preservation.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1769; current comparative cluster panel
