**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam kural and Kannada koral/koralcu independently establish both r and later l, including a close verbal extension.

**Direction.** Full southern forms favor kor-al-c before Telugu krōlcu; the final l does not result from duplication.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kur-al > *kor-al; *kor-al-c > *krōl-c > krōlcu, with krōlucu showing an additional medial vowel. Kannada korḷu is syncope without initial displacement, koḷḷu can assimilate r internally.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The exact order of verbal formation and contraction is reconstructed; krōlucu need not be the historically earlier surface variant. This is a better matched low-a formation than root-only comparisons.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1774; current comparative cluster panel

<a id="d1787"></a>
## d1787: blind

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1787 |
| Comparative input | *kur-uṭ-V; immediate *kur-ḍ-V |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | u / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | u |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u-ṭV / CVC-ḍV |
| Grammatical category | adjective/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Whole blindness stem supported independently; person endings do not add etyma; timing of V2 syncope remains inferential. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam kuruṭu and Kannada kuruḍu independently supply high-u disyllabic input. Tulu kurḍu and Kota kurḍ independently support the syncopated medial cluster, while Kannada kuḍḍu shows its assimilated alternative.

**Direction.** The full and syncopated southern series establishes k-u-r ordering. Telugu gruḍḍi/gruḍḍu has the rhotic before u; guḍḍi is attested beside it but cannot be mechanically generalized to every language with guḍḍi.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kur-uḍ-V > *kur-ḍ-V > *kru-ḍḍ-V > gruḍḍi/gruḍḍu > guḍḍi, with initial k/g alternation and later r loss. Strengthening might precede displacement; *kurḍḍ > kruḍḍ yields the same result. Contraction followed by shortening is another possible route. Final i/u and gender formations remain separate.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Identical u+u does not guarantee a long modern vowel: the independently attested consonantal branch is crucial. Initial g is not explained by naming the r/vowel exchange. Gondi/Kolami/Naikri guḍḍi could be Telugu loans or local medial assimilation; no observed cluster establishes independent metathesis there. Malto qoṭri may involve internal consonant reversal relative to kur-ṭ, but its precise morphology and quantity require separate study.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K61 §§1.142–154; K03 pp.130–131,157–162; DEDR 1787

<a id="d1818"></a>
## d1818: pit, hollow, tube, dig

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1818 |
| Comparative input | *ku/oẓ-i pit; *ku/oẓ-al/av tube; consonantal digging formations |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/a/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i / CVC-a-L / CVC-a-v / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | noun/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Pit -i, tube -al/-av and digging consonantal formations independently distinguished; no uniform low-a assignment. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuẓi pit contrasts with kuẓal/kuẓai tube; Malayalam kuẓa/kuẓal and Kannada koẓal/koẓavi independently establish low-a tube formations. Gondi koṛi and Konda kuṛk corroborate initial k-V-apical order.

**Direction.** Independent full southern/central forms support k-V-ẓ before Telugu kr and old kẓ. Different high/low and consonantal formations must not be collapsed to a single convenient *koẓ-a input.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Low-a *koẓ-al/av > *kẓōl/ōv > krōlu/krōvi, then kōlu. A consonantal *koẓ-cc > *kẓocc > kroccu explains short digging forms; old kẓōce has a distinct long variant. Kui kṛāu/Kuvi gṛāyu are displaced pit names with low outcome, but independently known pit *kuẓ-i is not the same low-a tube derivative. Exact pit-name -ay formation needs reconstruction.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** K80 explicitly contrasts Kui pit kṛāu and tube krōḍu; that semantic distinction describes distribution without itself explaining a sound condition. Kui krūpa has another vowel/formation. Telugu kukki/goppu could be direct medial assimilation; do not infer concealed metathesis merely from lost ẓ. Kannada kōvi is explicitly Telugu borrowing. The porridge *kūẓ reconstruction attached to this group is not evidence for a long pit input.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 pp.497–499 item 7; DEDR 1818; K61 pp.67–68 old kẓ clusters

## d1822: rot, become soft, decay

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1822 |
| Comparative input | *kuẓ-ay; *kuẓ-l? and other derivatives |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-ay / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core-formation-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuẓai, Malayalam kuẓayuka and Kannada koẓe independently support a medial approximant. Exact lateral formative behind Telugu ḷḷ is not supplied by these low-ay verbs.

**Direction.** Full southern approximant stems favor promotion in kruḷḷu, but the extra final lateral needs morphology or redistribution.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kuẓ-l > *kẓu-l > kruḷḷu, or a fuller derivative plus syncope, supplies a short consonantal route. kuḷḷu may lose cluster r or reflect direct medial assimilation.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep distinct from truḷḷu3364 with no independent r/ẓ. Gondi kukk and Kannada kocce can develop by medial assimilation; no concealed initial cluster is required. Low-a source formation does not independently verify the assumed lateral suffix.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1822; current comparative cluster panel

## d1826: sink, submerge, set

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Every apical-bearing reflex in the set is already clustered. A full cognate may be available in bend/sink1767, but that is an explicit cross-entry hypothesis.

**Direction.** Shared eastern clusters establish a regional stem, not the direction of an earlier vowel-r exchange.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Within Telugu kruŋku > guŋku/gūku can involve r loss, voicing and nasal loss/lengthening; the original *kur- stage remains conditional on1767 cognacy. Eastern ŋg/k transitivity and labial forms have distinct morphology.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not count this as an independent secure metathesis root while its full input is missing. Treat merger with1767 in sensitivity; phonetic and semantic support are stronger than an invented output-based proto-vowel.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d1850: pound, strike with fist

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuṟu:kuṟṟu, Kota kur:kut and Gondi kurkal independently establish an apical weak/strong family. Kannada gurdu provides a close r+d formation.

**Direction.** Kannada gurdu beside guddu and Telugu gruddu favors displacement of an earlier medial apical in at least the fist-striking formation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kur-d > *krud > gruddu with initial/suffix voicing and strengthening is plausible; guddu can be direct rd assimilation or later cluster-r loss. Labial kummu/guppu formations must be analyzed separately.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The many expressive impact words and ṯṯ/tt changes do not all share one literal r root. Telugu krummu is embedded in a gloss, not a separately linked form in this annotation. Source-level extraction could recover it without adding a root. Marathi guddā could reflect diffusion but does not decide it.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1850; current comparative cluster panel

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuṟu/kuṟai, Kannada kuṟu/koṟe and Konda kuṟi independently establish the full apical root; strong and nasal formations occur independently.

**Direction.** Kui kṛōpka plausibly continues displacement before a velar-labial derivative; Telugu kruyyu has an explicit competing assignment1778.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *koṟ-a-k > *krōk, then k+p > pk, gives Kui kṛōpka; kōpka/kōga can reflect r loss or distinct derivation. Telugu short y formation remains conditional on cognacy and suffix history.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Telugu retained kuṟu/kuṟuca and kundu must remain in the denominator; kruyyu is A in both entries. The head *kuṯ-ay is not the immediate source of every strong child/jackal formation. Source-corrupted Kota fragments are not separate phonological evidence.

## d1859: cut, reap, saw

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1859 |
| Comparative input | *ku/oṯ-ay; high-vowel and consonantal cut derivatives |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-ay / CVC-u / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Low-ay base independent; exact Kui labial formation reconstructed, historical Telugu noun is long. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuṟai and Malayalam kuṟekka independently support low-ay cutting formation; Kannada koṟe and the shorter Tamil kuṟu support additional vowel histories. Central Dravidian kud/kut forms support medial apical but not identical suffixes.

**Direction.** Southern/Central k-V-apical order supports earlier unshifted root. Kui krāpa has moved r before V; Old Telugu kōṟa remains V-before-r and is a long nominal formation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *koṯ-a-p > *krōp > krāp gives Kui krāpa under contraction then lowering; pre-contraction o>a is the competing order. Kannada korcu > koccu and Tulu koccu can arise by medial assimilation. Telugu kōṟa has a long vowel but no initial cluster and is not a displaced reflex.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** K80’s low-a comparison has independent southern support, but exact causative p formation and its vowel remain reconstructed. Do not apply the expected short-root change to the Old Telugu long noun without establishing its grade. Cutting, boring and fire-kindling meanings may converge with d2168; the source explicitly questions some Kannada comparisons.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 pp.497–499 item 8; DEDR 1859

## d1861: pierce, insert, prick

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kuṟṟu establishes an alveolar strong stem, not an independently short-vowel singleton with a following vowel. Gondi guhc/guˀc has no surviving rhotic.

**Direction.** Telugu gruccu plausibly reflects an apical-plus-palatal derivative, but the weak derivative required by an ordinary displacement account is not directly attested here.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *kuṯ-cc > *kṯu-cc > gruccu, or an earlier strong apical with partial redistribution and palatalization; guccu may be direct strong-stem development or later r loss.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A genuine structural residual: do not use the imported gru-cc proto-head to prove earlier clusters. Tamil ṟṟ can also be morphologically strengthened from a weak root, but that weak formation must be independently connected, possibly through1850.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d1898: sharp, pointed

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1898 |
| Comparative input | *kūr; Telugu krūru possibly Sanskrit krūra |

| V1 quality / quantity | ū / long |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/u |

| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil, Malayalam and Kannada kūr independently establish long ū and postvocalic r; Telugu krūru contains two rhotics, not a single exchanged r.

**Direction.** A literal kūr > krūr requires duplication or a second rhotic formative. Sanskrit krūra is a competing comparison: Monier-Williams1899 p.322 includes hard/solid and sharp senses. Direct Telugu transmission is still unverified, so no borrowing label is assigned.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible secondary initial r in kūru on Cr models, or a loan/semantic convergence with krūra. Telugu kūci/kūcamu reflect a palatal derivative without initial apical movement.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Neither a short *kur-u root nor a second inherited r is justified by the output. Long-vowel and segment-number anomaly kept A. Check older dictionary etymology and sharp/cruel semantics to distinguish borrowing and native remodeling.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 1898; current comparative cluster panel

## d1906: paddy, grain

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1906 |
| Comparative input | *kūl-i / *kūl-am |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | ū / long |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC-i / CVVC-am |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Long root independently present with both -i and -am; suffix difference does not create long quantity. |
| Input class | long-apical-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for regional long root; deeper borrowing uncertain |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | long-vowel-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kūlam and Konda/Kui/Kuvi/Pengo/Manda kūli independently support long ū before l, with distinct final formations.

**Direction.** The southern long root and eastern long forms agree on k-V-l order. No reconstructed short *kul is required by this set.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kūl-i > Kui kūḍi, Kuvi/Pengo/Manda kūli preserves order; l>ḍ does not depend on an earlier initial cluster. Brahui xōlum could match a different suffix and vowel history, but DEDR explicitly offers an Indo-Aryan alternative.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A long-vowel bound-formation control, unlike the doubly restricted free root kāl. Agricultural vocabulary can diffuse, so repeated eastern attestations do not alone prove inheritance; the relevant negative phonological observation remains long kūl rather than klū. Brahui xōlum is not a secure inherited vote because the source also compares Sanskrit godhūma through DBIA123. Do not confuse this entry with neighboring kūli wages1905.

**Mechanism scope.** Long-input retention; Brahui cognacy unresolved.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR1906; DEN1 1972 p.416 entryS278; PSS83 p.229

## d1959: scoop up

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d1959 |
| Comparative input | regional *ker-V; K80 proposes *ker-a |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V + labial/palatal formation |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Konda establishes the root, not the exact low formative proposed in K80. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | medium |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core-formation-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Konda ker independently supplies k-e-r order, but its stem notation ker- does not independently establish a following a. K80 reconstructs *ker-a from this comparison.

**Direction.** The full Konda root and initial gr in all other reflexes support displacement, with separate k>g. Direction of e/a quality change is an additional issue, not settled by consonant order.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *ker-a > *krē > grē, with Kui lowering to grā in one dialect; alternatively pre-contraction e>a before a yields grā. Kuvi grec, Pengo gre and Manda grepa preserve e. Exact labial/palatal formative and vowel quantities differ.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Kui grāpa/grēpa is a valuable dialect contrast, but cannot independently validate the reconstructed low V2 which helps explain it. No Telugu cognate is supplied. Do not count each language’s suffix as an independent root. The regional proto-level is more defensible than a pan-Dravidian *grä already containing the outcome.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 pp.496–499 item 1; DEDR 1959

**Independent input evidence.** Kui kēri and Brahui xēr establish long root, Parji keri a short full form; all place r after the vowel.

**Direction.** Telugu krē/krēva has r before ē, so a displacement-family interpretation is plausible, but long-root exchange versus short derived contraction is unresolved.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *ker-a-v > krēva lacks independent a/v support; alternative *kēr-V > krē involves a long root. krēgannu is a side-eye compound, not an independent event.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This remains a quantity/formation residual rather than confirmation of low-a conditioning. The widely separated Brahui comparison is useful for order but may have its own contact history; no source here labels the form a loan.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2008; current comparative cluster panel

## d2018: kindred, family, friend

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2018 |
| Comparative input | short *ki/eḷ-ay and long *kēḷ; Kui nominal -mbu formation |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/e / mixed by formation |
| C2 identity / structure | ḷ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-ay / CVVC / CVC-a-mb |
| Grammatical category | noun/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Short kiḷai and long kēḷ independently distinct; Kui nominal ending not inferred as part of a bare root. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kiḷai ramify/kindred and Kannada keḷe/geḷe independently establish a short low-formative series alongside Tamil kēḷ friend. Short vowel cannot be rejected merely because the dictionary headword selects long kēḷ.

**Direction.** Southern short and long forms have V before lateral; Kui klāmbu has initial cluster and additional nominal morphology. Direction of displacement is plausible independently of the long ā outcome.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *keḷ-a-mbu > *klēmbu > klāmbu is K80-type contraction then lowering; pre-contraction e>a is also possible. Plural klāpka has stem/number alternation with mb/pk, not a second independent metathesis root. Kannada geṇe/geṇiya and Tulu geṇe have medial lateral-to-nasal developments.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The exact -mbu formative should be checked against Kui nominal morphology; Tamil kiḷai alone does not supply it. K80 prints old DED 1628, but the correct old number is 1678 (modern2018); 1628 is do1957. Badaga kliūgidu is a plant name with a different Kannada comparison and is not evidence for lateral displacement in friend; its inclusion would manufacture an exception to southern distribution.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 pp.497–499 item 9, old-DED misnumbering; DEDR 2018

<a id="d2146"></a>
## d2146: fat, become fat, proud

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2146 |
| Comparative input | *koẓ-u; *koẓ-(u)-w / *koẓ-(u)-kk; long *kōẓ |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | o / short and independently long grade |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u / CVC-w / CVC-K / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | adjective/verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Labial fat noun and velar verb/noun separated; no low-a input independently established for these forms. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil koẓu/koẓuppu, Malayalam koẓu/koẓukka and Kannada korvu/korbu independently support o-ẓ and high-u/labial formations. Gondi koṛvinj and Konda koṛvu strengthen the short labial comparison; Tamil kōẓ is a separately attested long grade.

**Direction.** Southern, Gondi, Konda and central forms agree on k-o-apical. Telugu krovvu and Kui krōga instead place the apical next to k. The input labial versus velar extensions cannot be collapsed into one identical stem.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *koẓ-w > *kẓow > krovvu > kovvu gives Telugu schematically, with labial gemination a separate issue. Kui *koẓ-(u)-k > krōg gives a long mid vowel without the low ā found after independently low-a formations. Pengo kṛō and Manda kṛuva preserve different quantity/suffix histories. Kannada korbu > kobbu permits medial assimilation without an initial kr stage.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is a useful high-u comparison for eastern lowering, but exact u/zero in each immediate velar input is not supplied by the bare root alone. Toda kvāv/kvaḷp has initial k-v after loss/change of ẓ and a different vowel history; it is not evidence of the same k-r metathesis. Kuvi candle klōva is semantically plausible from fat/tallow yet requires source/contact scrutiny; kept uncertain. Related derivatives count as one family.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2146; K80 low-a lowering hypothesis; K03 Rule 21

<a id="d2149"></a>
## d2149: new, sprout, young; kinship derivatives

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2149 |
| Comparative input | *koẓ-utt-V; short *koẓ-V and long *kōẓ formations |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | o / mixed by formation |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u-tt / CVC-V / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | adjective/verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Short new adjective and short/long kinship formations must be separate input classes; exact tt extension is reconstructed, not identical to Tamil nt. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil koẓuntu, Malayalam koẓunnu, Gondi koṛs and Parji koṛ/koṛc independently establish k-V-apical order. K03 pp.159,198 distinguishes short *koẓ-utt-V new from short/long kinship formations.

**Direction.** Full southern and Central Dravidian forms support V before apical; Telugu krotta has changed order. Modern kotta is independently documented by K03 as the r-loss continuation, making concealed displacement demonstrable here.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *koẓ-utt-V > *koẓ-tt-V > *kẓott-V > krott-V > kotta is the proposed short branch. The tt belongs to the formation before metathesis in K03, not automatic new gemination. Telugu koḍuku preserves medial *ẓ > ḍ; kōḍalu has a long root grade. Kui kuṛa/kṛua and Kuvi koṛgi/kṛōgi show different formations and dialect outcomes.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Tamil koẓuntu has nt, not the identical tt formation: do not invent nt>tt to derive Telugu from Tamil directly. Exact *-utt support is the comparative reconstruction, whereas high-u formation is independently visible. Kui kṛua preserves two vowels and need not represent contraction; Kuvi long ō needs its own vowel/quantity history. Some kinship/nasal forms may have assimilated medially; neither those nor the related crop and kinship derivatives count as independent roots. Konda kodma is explicitly Telugu borrowing.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 pp.158–159 example 90, p.198 *koẓ-utt-V; DEDR 2149

<a id="d2176"></a>
## d2176: string, thread, arrange

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2176 |
| Comparative input | *kō; *kō-r/v/p derivative series |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | ō / long |
| C2 identity / structure | r/v/zero / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVV / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | long-input-derivative-r-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil kō:kōr and Kannada kō establish a long vowel-final root with variable extensions. Tamil/Malayalam kōrvai/kōrva have r and v, while kōvai lacks r.

**Direction.** Telugu krōva could promote derivative r, or add r to the kōva formation; the root is not independently a short CVr.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *kōr-v > krōv is long-vowel reordering; alternatively kōva > krōva by analogy. kōva may be retained r-less derivation or later r loss. The alternatives are observationally unresolved.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The productive-looking suffix alternants independently motivate a boundary, but not its age or order. This is excluded from secure D. Long nonrhotic derivatives across central languages cannot be read as concealed metathesis.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2176; current comparative cluster panel

**Independent input evidence.** Malayalam kōruka supplies long r, Kannada koḷḷu short strong lateral. Their relationship does not establish a uniform immediate input.

**Direction.** Telugu krōlu and Kuvi gronj are cluster forms, but Telugu has both r and l where neither full comparandum supplies both.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A *kor-al or *kōr-l derivative could produce krōlu, with different quantity histories, but neither suffix is independently attested. Kuvi gronj could reflect a different nasal derivative.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Retain A for exact cognacy/segment history rather than inventing a low-a suffix. Additional full r+l formation, dated Telugu or wider ingestion vocabulary would distinguish accounts.

## d2237: stick, shaft, long

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2237 |
| Comparative input | *kōl |
| Initial consonant | k |
| V1 quality / quantity | ō / long |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/a/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC / CVVC-V |
| Grammatical category | noun/adjective |
| Boundary evidence | Independently free root; later compounds and plurals do not make independent roots. |
| Input class | long-apical-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada and Konda kōl independently establish a long-vowel free root; Telugu kōla and eastern kōl/kōḍu continue that input.

**Direction.** The long vowel precedes the lateral across several branches. Toda initial kv contains a labial associated with the rounded vowel, not the displaced reflex of root-final l, whose fricative reflex remains after the vowel.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *kōl > kōla/kōlu retains order. Kui kōḍu and plural kōṭka change the medial/final lateral to a stop without promoting it. Toda kōl > kvɨ̄s̱ requires vowel breaking and lateral fricativization, not k-l metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A strong independent long/free-root control, including Kui/Kuvi plural formations that retain initial order. Short Gondi kola/Kolami kolā cannot establish original short V against the broad long comparison and may be local shortening. Many Badaga stick compounds and proper names are not independent etyma. The imported *kōy-il palace reconstruction is unrelated metadata, excluded.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2237; PSS83 pp.229–230 long/free-root restriction

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil and Malayalam caraṭu independently establish low a between r and retroflex ṭ; Kota carḍ supports a consonantal variant.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The exact initial consonant chronology is not fixed by the final tr alone. Central forms have regional contact plausibility but no explicit loan attribution here; classify their historical route A. One rope root despite multiple materials.

## d2359: snake, cobra, krait

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2359 |
| Comparative input | *car-a-(n)c(c)-; immediate Telugu *tar-a-ncc- |
| Initial consonant | c/t |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-(N)CC |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Independent nasal/geminate variant distinguished from simple final s; southern vu is later morphology. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for segment order; medium for exact common suffix |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Konda saras/sarasu and Gondi taras/taranj independently support initial s/t-a-r-a and a final s/nj alternation. Tamil ara/arā/aravu and Malayalam aravu agree in r following the first vowel but have lost initial c; they cannot alone reconstruct an originally vowel-initial root.

**Direction.** Konda and Gondi favor C-a-r before eastern Cr. Southern initial loss is independently comparable with broader c-loss correspondences, not evidence that Telugu added t. Tamil final ā is analyzed by K03 through -ac > -ah > ā, separately from first-syllable metathesis.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** K03 reconstructs *car-a-ncc > regional *tar-a-ncc > *trā-ncc > trā̃cu. Kui *sar-as > srāsu/srācu; Kuvi/Pengo *srāc > rāc with first-member loss. Manda trehe retains the initial cluster but changes final consonant/vowel. Nasal/geminate and simple-s variants require distinct immediate formations.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Direction is strongly comparative; exact shared innovation still depends on dating branch-specific s/t and suffix developments. Telugu nasal vowel and Gondi taranj support a nasal formation independently, while many cognates have no nasal. The Prakrit sarāhaya comparison in DEDR/K03 may reflect borrowing and is not an independent Dravidian denominator. Konda srāsu is quoted in K03 p.122 but absent from this database group; do not silently manufacture a database variant.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 pp.122–123 n.5(1); DEDR 2359; DNM sarāhaya cited there

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil cari/carukku, Kannada sari/saraku/jarugu and Tulu sarki/jari independently support full r order and consonantal derivatives.

**Direction.** Telugu sraggu plausibly promotes r from the sibilant series, while jarugu/caṟiya retain full order in other formations.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *sar-g > sraggu with suffix strengthening/voicing; saggu can follow r loss or direct rg assimilation. Full jarugu and sraggu need not have identical initial or formative histories.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** K61 probable early Kannada-loan class may apply to voiced geminates, but no individual loan proof is supplied here. Malto jarq retains order, showing velar suffigation does not by itself force reordering. Source crossreference snake2359 is not a root merger.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

<a id="d2456"></a>
## d2456: incline, side; disputed eastern descend

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2456 |
| Comparative input | *cāy; alternative eastern *i/eṟ-a (d516) |
| Initial consonant | c |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā / long in southern root; short under alternative eastern etymology |
| C2 identity / structure | y / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC / alternative VC-a |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Two competing roots are alternatives, not two independent eastern observations. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high southern; low eastern cognacy |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | alternative-cognacy-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil cāy, Malayalam cāyka and Telugu cāya independently support initial c with long ā and following glide. Eastern jāpa and Manda jē/hē can instead be compared with the descend root d516; their initial consonants and vowels do not settle cognacy by themselves.

**Direction.** The southern incline group has unambiguous c-ā-y order. K80 reassigns some eastern forms to *eṟ-a and a displacement/lowering history, while DEDR places them under cāy and cites Burrow1976 pp.40–41.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Southern *cāy > cāy/cāya and Malayalam āyka/āñcuka involves initial c loss and stem/tense changes, not apical transfer. If eastern *cāy-p is right, jāpa need not metathesize. If the d516 comparison is right, *eṟ-a-p > *ṟēp > jāpa involves displacement, lowering and apical-to-j; Manda jē/hē preserves a nonlow vowel and needs its own vowel history.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep the competing etymologies explicit; do not count the same Kui/Manda words once as retained incline and again as metathesized descend. Burrow1976 A sketch of Manda grammar in comparison with Pengo, Dravidian Linguistics V pp.39–56 has been identified, but pp.40–41 have not been read directly. Its argument is therefore not reconstructed from the citation. Needed: full Manda paradigm, comparative c/j versus ṟ/j correspondences and shared derivative morphology.

**Mechanism scope.** Southern retention; eastern cognacy determines whether any metathesis occurred.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR2456 and516; K80 pp.498–499; Burrow1976 pp.40–41 cited by DEDR, not directly consulted

## d2628: chironji tree and nut

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2628 |
| Comparative input | *cir/cēr-V?; regional *ser/ sar-ēk |
| Initial consonant | c/s |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/e/a / mixed, proto-quantity unresolved |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | e/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V-K / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Velar tree formation versus unsuffixed nut/tree root; no exact V2 class inferred from output. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | medium for order; low for exact vowels/quantity |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | regional-contact-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Kolami sire/cīre, Naikri śīre and Parji cīr independently support c-V-r but mix short/long grades. Gondi serkā/sirkā and sarēkā/saṛēka support a velar tree formation; exact V1/V2 before metathesis remains uncertain.

**Direction.** Multiple central and Gondi forms favor s-V-r before Kui srēko. The imported *srēk-o reconstruction adopts the shifted cluster and cannot be used to claim that Gondi inserted its vowel without independent argument.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *ser-V-k > srēk gives Kui; *srēk > rēk gives Kuvi/Pengo/Manda and some Gondi lects. Alternative regional borrowing of srēko/rēko is plausible for a culturally salient tree name. Long cīr and short serk cannot be collapsed to assert unrestricted long-vowel metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** No Telugu attestation in the linked corpus. The restricted geography and regional tree-name traffic weaken family-wide inheritance claims. Gondi full and r-initial variants preserve useful lect evidence, but distinct suffix vowels and quantity prevent a deterministic conditioning assignment. Latin B. latifolia is a parser fragment, not a Gondi word.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2628; Burrow–Emeneau 1972 DEN1 p.407 entry 2160; Southworth 2006 *cir/cīr

| Comparative input | *cup; *cow-ar/*cov-ar > *ow-ar |
| Initial consonant | c/zero |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | p/w / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC / CVw-ar |
| Grammatical category | noun/verb/adjective |

**Independent input evidence.** Central sup/cup preserves an initial consonant also reflected by Gondi savvar/hovar, while southern uppu and uvar independently support a stop versus intervocalic labial alternation and the low-a extended formation. Tamil uvar and Gondi havar/savvar are independent of the eastern long-vowel outcomes.

**Direction.** Comparative evidence favors an earlier full labial-containing *cow-ar/*ov-ar, not treating modern long sōr/sār as an original root. The r is already final in the extension and never becomes pre-vocalic in eastern forms.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *cow-ar > *cōr > Konda sōru, Pengo sōr, versus Kui sāru/Kuvi hāru/Manda jār involves intervocalic labial loss/contraction and eastern lowering. Lowering may precede contraction through *cawar or follow contraction of a low-a formation; the outputs alone do not determine which. Southern *ov-ar gives uvar/ogar, with Malayalam ōr showing an independent contraction parallel. Telugu vagaru may involve initial labial/prothetic or analogical restructuring, not established vowel-r metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is evidence about lowering in contracted roots, not an apical metathesis positive. It helps separate the two processes and avoids defining lowering by the presence of Cr. K80 p.498 prints Pengo hōr where DEDR gives sōr: preserve the source discrepancy, do not silently replace the database. Salt vocabulary can diffuse; the full southern/central contrast still independently establishes the earlier order. Nihali copo is a contact comparison, not a Dravidian language vote.

**Mechanism scope.** Labial loss/contraction; not initial apical metathesis.

**Scholarly references.** K80 p.498 item4; DEDR2674; K03 p.97 example10 (ogaru perhaps a Kannada loan; Gondi sawwor vowel metathesis)

## d2687: shrink, shrivel, wrinkle

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil curuŋku/curukku, Malayalam curuŋŋuka and Kannada surku independently establish medial r and full/consonantal formations.

**Direction.** Full r order in several branches favors Telugu srukku as innovative; surũgu retains the fuller sequence.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *cur-kk > *crukk > srukku, with initial c>s separate. Earlier *curu-kk can syncopate before displacement, whereas Kannada sukku/Malayalam cukkuka can assimilate medially without metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Brahui kurring retains postvocalic r and has a separately discussed irregular initial k; Emeneau1997 also queries kūžing with1876/2687, not a settled comparison. Marathi wrinkle vocabulary can show contact but is not an extra family vote.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2687; current comparative cluster panel; Emeneau1997 irregular sibilant discussion; queried kūžing excluded

## d2698: whirl, roll, revolve

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2698 |
| Comparative input | *cuẓ-i/a; initial-loss *uẓ-al and related formations |
| Initial consonant | c/zero |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i / CVC-a-l / VC-a-l |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Whirl *cuẓ-i versus roll *uẓ-al; initial c loss and long grade separately annotated. |
| Input class | uncertain-initial-order |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for uẓ-al order; medium for exact Telugu trajectory |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | conditional-displacement |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil cuẓi/cuẓal alongside uẓal, Malayalam cuẓaluka/uẓaluka, and Kannada suẓi/toẓal/uẓal independently support both c-initial and initial-loss families, with a second lateral in the roll formation. Telugu suḍi retains the first type; ḍollu is compared with the second.

**Direction.** Several branches establish vowel before ẓ and a following l in uẓal, giving a much stronger potential direction for roll ḍollu than for homophonous fall d2988. Initial c loss is independently attested, although whether it preceded displacement in Telugu itself is not directly dated.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *cuẓ-al > *uẓ-al > *oẓ-al > *ẓōl > ḍollu requires contraction followed by shortening/gemination, or an earlier syncope route with a consonantal derivative. K61 p.54 §1.127 discusses alternative suffix/quantity histories. Telugu suḍi continues *cuẓ-i without displacement. Kui ḍuṛi retains an apical after u and may have initial c>ḍ plus a medial rhotic; its initial ḍ is not sufficient evidence of the vowel-initial pathway.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Telugu roll is a plausible displacement family, but exact input and collision with regional fall ḍollu d2988 prevent a strict mechanism claim. A pathway cẓ > ẓ after displacement would give the same surviving initial segment as c loss before displacement; chronology is not forced. Several Telugu fragments split ḍol(u)cu into bogus forms; restore only in source supplement, preserve raw data. Gondi uḍ/uḍḍ has medial change and retains initial u.

**Mechanism scope.** Plausible roll displacement with quantity alternatives and potential lexical convergence.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2698; K61 p.54 §1.127 (prior page verification); original DEDR SQL rows 63979–63999; compare DEDR 2988

<a id="d2883"></a>
## d2883: flow, pour, drip; blood/drop

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2883 |
| Comparative input | *cor/tar? regional *cur/tor with short and long grades; labial drop derivative |
| Initial consonant | c/t |
| V1 quality / quantity | o/u / short and long grades |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/u/a / unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V / CVVC / CVC-m-p |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for full r order; conditional for exact drop stem |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | brahui-displacement-comparison |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil cori/cura/cōr and tōr, Kannada suri/sōr/tore, Kota corv/toyr and Telugu torūgu/torāgu/toṟãgu establish full vowel-before-r order with several initial and quantity correspondences.

**Direction.** Brahui curring retains full order whereas trump/tramp have r before the vowel. PSS83 p.245 treats drop as a stronger metathesis example than simple aphaeresis, because output vowel is not the expected second i.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A pre-Brahui full *tur/tor-V-mp > *tr-V-mp > trump/tramp is a displacement-family comparison. Exact V2, t/c development and a/u outcomes are not jointly established; the modern Telugu long suffix vowels are not automatically the Brahui input. Parji cōrp > cōp illustrates direct medial r loss. Toda tvar has a preceding glide but r remains after a.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The traditional seven-item Brahui sample calls most roots t-initial, but this family has independently attested c/t variants, so a categorical Proto-Dravidian c exclusion is not justified. Telugu jobbillu is opaque assimilation or questionable cognacy, not positive metathesis. Markodi cre blood beside core-like forms is a fresh possible local syncope/displacement comparison, not automatically the old Telugu change. Konda sō- has an alternative d2867 link. A compound torgi stranded in a gloss still needs original-page recovery.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR2883; PSS83 pp.244–245 citing Emeneau1971 pp.192–194

## d2929: fire, blaze, live coal

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2929 |
| Comparative input | *nir-/ner-; labial *nir/ner-upp and velar derivatives |
| Initial consonant | n |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u-PP / CVC-V / CVC-K |
| Grammatical category | noun/verb |
| Boundary evidence | Labial noun and velar/intransitive verbs separate; relationship to vowel-initial burn uncertain. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for n-V-r; medium for exact vowels/formations |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil neruppu, Malayalam nerippu, Gondi nirvānā and Parji nir independently support n-V-r, with i/e and labial/velar formative variation. Neither imported *nijur nor **nirVvV is treated as uniquely established.

**Direction.** Several branches retain initial n-V-r. Telugu nippu lacks r; Kui drē instead has r immediately after a stop that may continue n through denasalization.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Telugu *nir-pp > nipp via medial r-p assimilation is sufficient; a hidden *nripp > nipp trajectory remains possible but unproved. Kui *nir-V > *nrē > drē combines displacement/contraction and n>d, with exact ancient V2 unresolved. Kurux niyū̃r requires additional medial vowel/glide history and is not simple evidence for the same immediate input.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The geminate labial environment alone does not certify Telugu metathesis: nippu is opaque without an attested nr/dr intermediate. This is a crucial comparison with trippu and krovvu. Related burning eri d811 may involve nasal prothesis/loss, but that deeper union remains a sensitivity hypothesis. Initial n is independently recoverable here and must not be removed to make a vowel-initial metathesis case.

**Mechanism scope.** Opaque Telugu medial reduction; eastern displacement with denasalization.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2929; K03 Rule 21 denasalization; comparison DEDR 811

<a id="d2988"></a>
## d2988: fall, lie down, die

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d2988 |
| Comparative input | *ḍol-/ḍul- (regional); relationship to ūḍu unresolved |
| Initial consonant | ḍ |
| V1 quality / quantity | o/u / short |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVC / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Regional root and long vowel-initial alternative not assumed identical. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-other-apical |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | medium; regional reconstruction, deeper source unresolved |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | lookalike-unresolved |

**Independent input evidence.** Gondi, Kolami and Kui/Kuvi independently have initial ḍ/d before the vowel and a following lateral or its loss. The lone Telugu ūḍu has a different shape and long vowel, insufficient to reverse the comparative direction for the whole family.

**Direction.** Broad regional agreement favors earlier ḍ-V-l for this set; there is no independently attested common *uḍal input here. Telugu ūḍu may be a related different formation, analogical associate or separate cognate hypothesis.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *ḍol > ḍollu/ḍol, and *ḍol-p > ḍōpa with lateral loss/assimilation and compensatory quantity, are local candidate developments. Deriving all initial ḍ from vowel/apical exchange would require independent evidence not supplied by these reflexes.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Initial retroflexion is not a metathesis diagnosis. The near-homophonous rolling forms in d2698 may have converged with this fall/death set, but conflating them would falsely supply a southern unshifted cognate. Long ūḍu versus short ḍul- deserves dictionary/historical morphology work; for now code its direction uncertain. No confirmed metathesis count from this entry.

**Mechanism scope.** Initial-retroflex lookalike; no established earlier reversed order.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 2988; compare DEDR2698 and K61 p.54 §1.127 alternative derivations (prior verified reading)

## d3014: remain, stay, be obtained

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3014 |
| Comparative input | *taŋ-k / *tak-k |
| Initial consonant | t |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | nonapical / singleton |
| Following vowel | u |
| Root/formation shape | CVNK / CVKK |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Velar/nasal stem formations independently supported. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | nonapical-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil taŋku/takku, Malayalam taŋŋuka/takkuka, Kannada taŋgu/dakku and central tak independently establish initial t and a velar/nasal medial cluster. No postvocalic apical is reconstructed.

**Direction.** Initial t/d/ḍ precedes a in all relevant cognates. Telugu ḍakku does not show reversal of an independently reconstructible *aḍ input.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tak-k > takku/dakku/ḍakku involves initial voicing/retroflexion or lexical variant association; *taŋ-k > taŋgu/tagg involves nasal/velar developments. These are distinct from initial vowel/apical displacement.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A false-positive control for searching Telugu initial ḍ. K61 p.53 §1.126 proposes hyperstandard ḍ for d in ḍakku; this is an alternative to metathesis, not a demonstrated ancient sound law. The same discussion finds no evidence for an assumed lost nasal source. Uncertainty about this consonant is not positive metathesis evidence. Related takku/takkin(a) morphology and cognates support the original t-initial analysis.

**Mechanism scope.** Initial voicing/retroflexion, not metathesis.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3014; K61 p.53 §1.126 (prior verified reading)

**Independent input evidence.** Parji terip/terit independently gives full apical order; Telugu tari/tarucu/tarcu provides an internal full/consonantal series.

**Direction.** Full Parji and Telugu forms favor tar-c before traccu; a bare protoform alone contributes no extra evidence.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tar-c > *tra-c > traccu with strengthening is plausible; tarucu could be a fuller ancestor or a separately vocalized derivative. Parji labial p differs from Telugu palatal c.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A good directional comparison with uncertain exact suffix-vowel chronology. Churning milk and fire-drilling can share rotary motion, but their semantic extension does not itself explain which formation changed. Retained tarcu shows that a consonantal stem is not sufficient for obligatory movement.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3095; current comparative cluster panel

**Direction.** Gondi taṛm favors earlier t-a-apical before Telugu trampi. Kui dlāva has a different labial vowel-bearing derivative and an explicitly proposed alternative aẓal etymology.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The database Kui aṛ̆al, *c and *t are editorial comparison fragments, not lexical attestations. Kui alternative276 must not be counted twice; its outcome stays A here. Telugu tanuku requires a different nasal/velar history.

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil taṛ̆ai and Malayalam taṛ̆a/taṛ̆ekka plus Kannada taṛ̆e establish medial apical order; vowel alternants and strong extensions are independent of Brahui.

**Direction.** Full southern stems and Kui dalga favor earlier t-V-apical versus Brahui trikking/trikk. The exact Brahui suffix vowel is not independently recovered.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *taẓ-V-kk > *tẓV-kk > trikk is a plausible displacement-family sequence, with apical merger to r. If V2 was i, simple loss of V1 would also yield trik-; if low a, additional vowel change is needed. The available data do not decide.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** PSS83 p.245 includes this among examples compatible with aphaeresis. Do not invent a high-i formative solely to derive the observed i. Brahui trikking is homophonous with d3244 wither but the two comparative roots and meanings remain separate pending evidence for a semantic bridge.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d3122: dig, excavate, scratch

**Independent input evidence.** Gondi taṛānā/tark and Kuvi taṛj independently retain full order; Kuvi taṛj:tṛaj gives a close internal formation contrast. Other branches have long tāṛ grades.

**Direction.** The close Kuvi pair and full Gondi root favor t-V-apical before Telugu travvu; r-only eastern forms can lose the first cluster consonant.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *taẓ-v > *tẓav > travvu > tavvu with labial strengthening and later r loss; Kuvi taṛj > tṛaj has the same directional relation with a palatal suffix. Konda ṟeb/Kuvi ṛev/Pengo ṛav can follow C1 loss, but e/o variants require distinct vowel histories.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A shared regional displacement pattern is plausible; exact v/b/j formation and long/short chronology are not one uniform word history. Kolami/Naikri tavv may reflect Telugu contact or internal apical loss; neither is independently demonstrated.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3122; current comparative cluster panel

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tāṇṭu and matching Malayalam/Kannada forms independently support long ā and nasal-stop cluster; Telugu dā̃ṭu and Konda ḍāṭ agree after nasal loss.

**Direction.** No comparative medial r supports deriving Brahui traḍḍing by the ordinary apical-exchange process.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tāṇṭ > Telugu dā̃ṭu/Konda ḍāṭ can proceed by initial voicing and nasal loss. Brahui traḍḍing requires unexplained r insertion/restructuring, a different reconstruction, borrowing or false cognacy; one-for-one metathesis is not established.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is an explicit long nasal-cluster comparison, not a positive merely because Br has tr-. The Sanskrit tāṇḍava comparison has unresolved borrowing direction. Independent evidence for an r-bearing pre-Brahui stem would change the diagnosis.

**Independent input evidence.** Parji tār and Gadaba tārg independently supply full long-vowel order. Their transmission history is not established by the dictionary grouping.

**Direction.** If inherited comparanda, tār-g precedes Telugu trāg; deriving a universal short *tar-ag from Telugu alone would be circular.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *tār-g > trāg is long-vowel displacement; alternatively a short vowel-bearing derivative first contracted, or central full forms arose by adaptation of a loan. Telugu trāvu has medial velar weakening and nouns add morphology.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The surface comparison strongly favors a historical relationship but leaves exact earlier quantity and inheritance/contact unresolved. No low-a suffix is independently attested. Gadaba sark requires separate initial and quantity correspondence.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3174; current comparative cluster panel

## d3195: sift, winnow

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3195 |
| Comparative input | *taṟ- / *tāṟ-; proposed Brahui *tar-añc- |
| Initial consonant | t |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short and long independent grades |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i / unknown formative |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V / CVVC / CVC-NC |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |

| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for root order, conditional for exact displaced formative |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | brahui-displacement-comparison |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil short taṟi and long tāṟṟu/tāttu, Tulu sāruni and Telugu tālucu establish full t/s-a-apical order with independent quantity alternants. Newly reported Brahui tāring preserves that order.

**Direction.** Brahui tāring and southern full roots favor derivation of dranzing/drãzing within the same sift family; they do not independently attest the exact proposed short *tarañc stem.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Emeneau proposes *tarañc- > *trañc- > dranz-/drāz-, with displacement-family contraction or aphaeresis, initial voicing and nasal/affricate changes. The long retained tāring is a different formation/grade, not necessarily the immediate input to dranz-.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Emeneau 1997 p.445 §12 removes the older query and rejects placement under d3402 *tūr as less economical. The original database drãzing spelling is preserved, not silently changed into drāzing. The -añc vowel is reconstructed, not independently supported by Tamil taṟi, so this does not prove a low-V2 law. Pengo dalŋgi ki has a different cluster/formative. Do not count the two Brahui derivatives as two roots.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR3195; Emeneau1997 p.445 §12; Emeneau1971 pp.192–194 cited by 1997, not directly obtained

## d3244: wrinkle, wither, be dried up

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3244 |
| Comparative input | *tir-aŋ/k; *tir-ay |
| Initial consonant | t |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tiraŋku/tirakku/tirai and Malayalam tira independently establish i-r-a order. Kannada tere, Kodagu tere and Telugu tera agree with full order after vowel developments.

**Direction.** Brahui trikking retains i after r. Simple deletion of first i from independently supported *tirakk would give trakk, making this a stronger vowel-preservation argument than same-vowel cases.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tir-a-kk > *tri-a-kk > trikk is a possible literal-exchange plus vowel-loss derivation. Assimilation of the two vowels followed by loss of the first also remains possible; the comparison establishes displacement-family history more securely than its phonetic implementation.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** PSS83 p.245 identifies wither and drop as stronger metathesis cases. The precise relation of nasal tiraŋku, strong tirakku and nominal tirai must remain morphological. Brahui trikking sprout d3119 is not counted as the same root solely on homophony.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR3244; PSS83 pp.244–245

<a id="d3246"></a>
## d3246: turn, return, twist, wander

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3246 |
| Comparative input | *tir-i/u; *tir-u-pp; *tir-u-kk; nasal and low-a derivatives |
| Initial consonant | t |
| V1 quality / quantity | i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/u/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u-K / CVC-u-PP / CVC-u-KK / CVC-V-NK |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Singleton velar, geminate labial/velar, nasal and low-a derivatives independently differentiated by southern morphology. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for matched high-vowel formations; medium for eastern low-a input |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tiri/tiruku/tiruppu/tirukku and Kannada tiri/tirugu independently establish high-vowel root and distinct singleton velar, geminate labial and geminate velar formations. Kannada tiragu/tirapa and Kodagu teraŋg additionally attest low-a formations; no one V2 fits all derivatives.

**Direction.** Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Gondi, Konda and central retained forms agree on t-i-r before Telugu tr-. Telugu itself contrasts retained tirugu and displaced trippu/trikku. The grammatical contrast is independently supported by Tamil intransitive and causative formations.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tir-upp > *tir-pp > *tri-pp > trippu; *tir-ukk > *tir-kk > *tri-kk > trikku, with equal-vowel syncope/reassociation not requiring a literal audible vowel swap. *tir-uk > tirugu retains order. Kui trēba and Kuvi rēnai involve a different formative and initial t loss in the latter; its exact low-a/ high-i input must not be inferred solely from ē. Manda trīmba matches a nasal formation with long quantity.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A strong independently formed Telugu contrast: singleton-velar turn is retained while geminate causative/twist forms displace. This is evidence for morphological/cluster conditioning within a family, not a universal rule until other geminate and singleton inputs are tested. Trimmaṭa/trimmaru wandering need exact derivational reconstruction and are flagged less certain than trippu. Central tipp may result directly from medial r-p assimilation; Telugu tipiri may be analogical or metathetically restructured but does not prove initial tr loss. Badaga Tirikōṇa is a proper name and should not be an extra inherited turn witness.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3246; K03 Rule 21; PSS83 p.229 nonautomatic application

<a id="d3259"></a>
## d3259: open

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3259 |
| Comparative input | *ti/eṯ-a; velar, labial and palatal extensions |
| Initial consonant | t |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a / CVC-a-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Low-a root independently attested; local labial/palatal extensions and input grades separate. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tiṟa, Kannada teṟa/teṟe and Malayalam tuṟakka independently establish a low-a formative and t-V-apical order. Telugu teṟacu/teṟa retains that independently supported environment.

**Direction.** Full southern forms and Konda Gūṛi teṟe support t-V-apical before Konda ṟe. Initial loss alone from teṟa would give ṟa, so the mid vowel in ṟē/jē requires prior vowel interaction or a different independently established formation.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *teṯ-a > *tṟē > ṟē gives Konda; later apical change gives Pengo/Manda jē and Kuvi de. Kui dāpa adds low outcome (contraction then lowering or lowering then contraction). Telugu teṟacu retains initial order, and suffix cu requires its own historical morphology.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A clear low-a retained Telugu family versus broader eastern displacement. Gondi rehānā may show first-member loss, but its own suffix/vowel and donor history remain uncertain. Tulu jappuni/depp could involve medial assimilation plus initial t>j/d, not necessarily the same metathesis; Kurux/Malto tisg likewise preserves the first vowel despite loss/change of apical. Toda key tɨrp is explicitly alternatively compared with turn d3246 or Tamil borrowing and cannot be treated as an independent ordinary open reflex.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 p.160 example 94; K80 pp.497–499 item 10; DEDR 3259

## d3305: cut into pieces, fragment

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3305 |
| Comparative input | *tuṇ-i/u; long *tūṇ formation |
| Initial consonant | t |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/ū / short and long formations |
| C2 identity / structure | ṇ / nasal |
| Following vowel | i/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | alternative-cognacy-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tuṇi, Kannada tuṇuku and Telugu tuniya independently establish a nasal root; no rhotic is required by this core comparison.

**Direction.** Telugu truŋgu/truncu could have secondary r in nasal formations, or belong to3339 tura. The dictionary explicitly preserves that alternative.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tuṇ-i-C > tuniy/tunc by nasal-place and suffixal changes is nonmetathetic. A rhotic-root derivation of truŋgu/truncu belongs to the competing analysis, not a demonstrated ṇ>r metathesis here.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The long beam *tūṇ does not replace short cut-root quantity. Assign contested Telugu forms A under both entries; collapse for sensitivity if desired, but no double D vote. Kuvi tũrhali may have a secondary rhotic and remains uncertain.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3305; current comparative cluster panel

## d3339: bore, pierce, scrape

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3339 |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tura/turuvu, Kannada turi and Tulu turiyuni independently support full r order. The source head long **tūr does not erase these short forms.

**Direction.** Full southern and northern comparisons favor eastern tr-; Telugu disputed cut/break forms also occur under3305 tuṇi.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Consonantal *tur-k > truk gives Konda tṟuk and Kui trupka after a separate k+p reversal. Kui trunga/trūva have distinct nasal/labial quantity histories. Telugu tuṟumu retains the full root; truŋgu/truncu remain alternative-cognacy cases.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not assign the same Telugu forms as secure D in two roots. Kui tuspa may follow r loss or direct simplification, not certain shared chronology. Long Kurux tūrnā is a regional grade, not evidence all short derivatives are secondary.

**Direction.** The full southern/central order favors innovation of trōyu/trōcu/trōlu and Kui/Kuvi trō-.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *tor-a-y/c/l > trōy/c/l, with low-a root supported but exact suffixes distinct. *tor-b > trobb/drobb gives a short voiced-geminate derivative; dobbu can be later r loss or imported/assimilated form. Gondi ro- can lose C1 after a cluster.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Kannada/Tulu dobbu and Naikri ḍʰobb make early contact plausible for the voiced-geminate subformation, not proven for every pushing word. The various Telugu suffixes and meanings remain one family, with a separate quantity test for each.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Direction.** Full tur order favors Telugu truppu/trukku as displaced-family formations. Southern tuppu/tukku show that direct medial assimilation can also remove r.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *tur-pp > truppu and *tur-kk > trukku; full *tur-upp/ukk plus syncope is an alternative. Telugu tuppu may be later r loss or an independently assimilated form.

**Independent input evidence.** Kurux tuṛᵘxnā and related forms supply a full t-u-r sequence independently of Brahui trukking.

**Direction.** The geographically separated Kurux full stem versus Brahui trukking favors reduction/displacement in Brahui. Superscript u in Kurux transcription must not automatically be treated as a full independent suffix vowel.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tur-(u)-k > *tru-k > trukk is the comparison. Literal u/r exchange and loss of initial u from a two-u stem cannot be distinguished without establishing the status of the Kurux superscript vowel and the pre-Brahui stem.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** PSS83 p.245 lists this among cases compatible with aphaeresis. Only two northern branches attest the reviewed family; no Telugu denominator vote arises from their presence.

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tuḷḷu, Malayalam tuḷḷuka, Kannada tuḷḷu, Kodagu tuḷḷ and Tulu tuḷḷuni independently establish a geminate lateral with no additional rhotic.

**Direction.** The widespread southern form and Telugu tuḷḷu favor earlier t-u-ḷḷ. Telugu truḷḷu retains that whole sequence and adds r, so ordinary transposition cannot derive it without an extra unsupported ancestral rhotic.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tuḷḷ-u > tuḷḷu; secondary literary r gives truḷḷu and its derivatives. K61 p.131 n.80 proposes hyperstandardization on the model of archaic Cr forms. This is a source proposal with strong segment-count evidence for addition, less direct evidence for its social mechanism.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A central negative control: initial tr does not guarantee metathesis. It is inappropriate to reconstruct **tur-uḷḷ solely from the Telugu outcome. Gondi tul could have simplified gemination or be related through contact; neither supplies the missing r. K61 citation was visually checked in the prior investigation; this run’s attempt to reopen p.131 reached the authorized preview limit and did not independently reverify the page.

**Mechanism scope.** Secondary r; hyperstandardization plausible, not metathesis.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 3364; K61 p.131 n.80 (prior run page verification, reopened preview unavailable)

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tuṟu/tuṟumu/tuṟumpu and strong tuṟṟu, Malayalam tuṟuka and Kannada tuṟugu/tuṟagu independently establish u before an apical and several following formations.

**Direction.** Full southern and central stems support derivation of Brahui trujjing from a fuller t-u-apical stem; the affricate formative does not have an exact independently matched full stem here.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *tuṯ/ṟ-u-C > *tṯ/ṟu-C > trujj- is a displacement-family hypothesis; same-u aphaeresis remains possible. Telugu tuṟugu/turugu and tuṟumu/turumu retain order. Strong tukku/tuttu and eastern cuc/tuc can arise by medial assimilation and are not automatic evidence for concealed initial metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** PSS83 p.245 includes this among aphaeresis-compatible examples. ṯ versus ṟ and affricate development require independent correspondence reconstruction; assigning a unique apical from the outcome would overstate the data. Strong and weak formations are kept in one root family with mixed input structure.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR3367; PSS83 pp.244–245

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil tū/tūval and Kannada tuppuẓ/tuppaẓu support different root/extension shapes. The Kannada apical occurs after pp, not directly after the first vowel.

**Direction.** Telugu truppuḍu has an initial r and final ḍ; simple adjacent V-r exchange from the closest Kannada form does not preserve the segment inventory.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A longer-distance apical shift plus final suffix remodeling is possible, as is secondary r added to a tuppuḍu-type derivative. Gondi tōṛ offers an apical root but not the complete pp-ḍ formation.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not suppress final ḍ or silently move the sole Kannada ẓ across pp while retaining a replacement. The dragonfly compounds are semantically/morphologically different and not additional evidence. Need historical feather forms and comparative suffix analysis.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

## d3402: winnow, scatter, sprinkle

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d3402 |

| Overall confidence | medium |
