| Root/formation shape | CVC-a / CVC-a-NK / CVC-u-K |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Low-a and high-u formations independently distinguishable; matched lost/transitive nasal/velar comparison across eastern languages. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil maṟa/maṟai, Malayalam maṟakka/maṟayuka and Kannada maṟe/maṟagu establish m-a-apical-a independently. Gondi māraŋg/mareŋg and Konda marg support a nasal/velar lost/hide formation.

**Direction.** Full southern and Gondi/Konda forms support original m-V-apical. Telugu maṟacu/maṟũgu retains that order, while Kui mrāŋga promotes the apical into a cluster.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *maṯ-aŋk > *mṟāŋg > Kui mrānga. Kuvi/Pengo jāŋg and Manda dāŋg are derived by DEDR through *mṟāŋg > *mjāŋg > jāŋg (with Manda apical d); these intermediate clusters are reconstructed, unlike attested Kui mr-. Separate causative mrāk-p > mrāp-k produces Kui mrāpka. Gondi ractāl is explicitly derived by the source from *mṟac with initial m loss.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Low-a does not compel Telugu displacement. Different maṟa-cu, maṟu-k and maṟa-ŋ formations must remain distinct before interpreting exact exceptions. Eastern j/d stems support shared development more strongly when nasal/velar morphology agrees, but do not by themselves prove every language inherited an identical completed sound change. Southern and central mak/maŋ/meŋ reductions may be medial assimilation; do not force hidden mr stages. Tamil source ṛ in maṛa is a transcription inconsistency beside its clear ṟ derivatives.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 4760 and explicit *mṟāŋg>*mjāŋg note; PSS83 p.229 lexical nonapplication principle

## d4761: turn over, return, be distressed, fall

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4761 |
| Comparative input | *maṯ-i/u; *maṯ-aŋk; *maṯ-al |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/u/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i / CVC-u-K / CVC-a-NK / CVC-a-l |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | High-i/u, low-a nasal and second-lateral formations separately reconstructed. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for root family; medium for exact Telugu formation |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil maṟi, maṟuku, maṟaŋku and Malayalam maṟiyuka/maṟukuka independently establish several formative vowels. Kannada maral/maraḷ and Telugu maralu support a second-lateral formation.

**Direction.** Full southern and eastern root forms establish m-a-apical before Telugu mraŋgu/mrandu. The meanings perish/decrease overlap other m-r roots, so exact linkage must be tested rather than inferred from spelling.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A short high-u/zero nasal or stop formation *maṯ-NK/ND > mraŋgu/mrandu is possible. If the exact input is instead Tamil low-a *maṟaŋku, short Telugu a requires later shortening after contraction. Telugu maralu > maḷḷu can result from medial r-l assimilation, with no initial mr stage. Kui mag-b > mabg reverses suffix consonants after a separate medial apical loss.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The short Telugu nasal-cluster outcome is not a deterministic confirmation until its V2 is fixed independently. Mraŋgu/mraggu may reflect convergence with d4750; preserve separate lexical affiliations and flag double-count risk. Kannada malar beside maral reverses the two liquids internally, a different process from initial vowel/apical displacement. Tulu marakaṇɛ/maraŋkaṇɛ is explicitly alternatively linked to d4740 and remains uncertain.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 4761; DEN1 1972 p.413 entry3898; compare DEDR 4750 and 4740

<a id="d4806"></a>
## d4806: bamboo, thorny bamboo

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4806 |
| Comparative input | regional *māṇ/ṛ-i; Kuvi mṇāhu formation |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā / long independently established |
| C2 identity / structure | ṇ/ṛ / nasal/rhotic singleton; immediate suffixal s cluster inferred |
| Following vowel | i / unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC-i / CVVC-s? |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Kuvi singular h versus plural sk; full i-ending noun is a different formation. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for long vowel and full order; medium for segment and formation |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | late-kuvi-long-apical-variable |

**Independent input evidence.** Kui māṇi/māṛi and Kuvi Ḍ. māṛi, S. mādi independently support a long vowel before an apical. Their nasal/rhotic/dental correspondences do not determine one uniquely original apical identity.

**Direction.** The full Kui and Kuvi forms favor m-ā-apical before Isr. mṇāhu. The ṇ could reflect promotion of an older nasal or assimilation of a promoted liquid next to m; these are distinct analyses.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *māṇ-s > *mṇā-s > mṇāhu (plural mṇāska), with an h/s stem alternation, provides a displaced nasal formation. Alternatively *māṛ-s > *mṛā-s > mṇā-s adds liquid-to-nasal assimilation. The s-formative is inferred from the Kuvi paradigm, not directly matched to full māṛi.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The long input is independently supported, so this is outside the narrow short-vowel Telugu domain. Exact noun formation and nasal chronology remain uncertain. Thorny bamboo versus a generic bamboo bush could reflect lexical specialization or borrowing. The dictionary explicitly removes Kurux mās as a pronunciation of Indo-Aryan bā̃s; it cannot be used as a northern cognate.

**Mechanism scope.** Long apical displacement-family; nasal before/after reordering unresolved.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR4806; DED(S)3929; Pfeiffer1972 correction cited in source

<a id="d4831"></a>
## d4831: die, cease, extinguish, erase

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4831 |
| Comparative input | *māḷ; short *maḷ-a/u-NK; regional *maṇ-k |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā/a / independent long root and short derivatives |
| C2 identity / structure | ḷ/ṇ / lateral/nasal; short consonantal formations |
| Following vowel | a/u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC / CVC-V-NK / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Short/long grade and transitive/intransitive formations independently distinguishable, exact nasal chronology unknown. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for full order; medium for grades; low for e outcome |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | late-kuvi-mixed-quantity-secondary-nasal |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil māḷ and Kannada māḷ independently establish a long lateral root. Tamil maṭku, Telugu malugu/malãgu/manũgu and Kuvi maṇk support shorter and nasal formations independently; the short grade is not invented from the displaced outcome.

**Direction.** Southern m-V-lateral forms and retained Kuvi maṇk favor m-V-apical before mṇeŋg/mṇek. Nasal identity has independent regional support but cannot simply replace the deeper lateral.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Short *maḷ-k > *maṇ-k > *mṇak, or *maḷ-k > *mḷak > *mṇak, are alternatives preceding Kuvi mṇek; the a>e quality remains unexplained. The intransitive nasal-velar mṇeŋg contrasts with stronger mṇek. F. mṛakʰali has r and a and may preserve a different assimilation/quality history. Telugu retains mal/man order through its short and long formations.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Kuvi e is a genuine residual, not a reason to reconstruct unsupported *meṇ. DEDR assigns these forms to the same family; the exact short-grade derivation, semantics and source differences need a fuller paradigm. Badaga buru māle naked has insufficient semantic evidence and is not counted as a cognate. Nasal/stop alternation in Tamil māḷ:māṇṭ is a morphological control, not initial metathesis.

**Mechanism scope.** Displacement-family supported, with unresolved a/e quality and secondary nasal chronology.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR4831, DED3958; source labels in panel-030

## d4855: Anogeissus tree

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4855 |
| Comparative input | regional *miṇ-iya |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṇ / nasal |
| Following vowel | i |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i-yV |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Full miṇiya independently attested, but lexical suffix segmentation unproven. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for immediate segment order, medium for common inheritance |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | late-kuvi-short-nasal |

**Independent input evidence.** Pengo and Manda miṇiya independently give short i before nasal and i after it; Kuvi mṇīya is the displaced comparison. The database *mṇīj head follows the outcome and is not accepted as the earlier order.

**Direction.** Two full regional forms support miṇ-i over an inherited initial mṇ followed by two separate identical epentheses; tree-name borrowing remains an alternative source of the geographical pattern.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible *miṇ-iya > *mṇiiya > mṇīya, consistent with same-vowel contraction after nasal reordering. Literal exchange versus first-vowel loss and compensatory length is not uniquely proven by this set.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is a nasal-input case, unlike eel4737 where independent full forms have l. The sparse regional botanical comparison needs better species/dialect records, and the Kuvi database gloss loses an independent F. full form if any existed: only the printed Pengo/Manda evidence is asserted here. No Telugu attestation is a missing cell, not retention.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR4855; PSS83 p.232 n.5, DEDS785

## d4866: swallow

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4866 |
| Comparative input | *miẓ-u-nk; regional *miẓ-i-nk and mu/v variants |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/i |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V-NK |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Nasal-velar extension independently supported, with u/i V2 variants; no new geminate needed for existing NK cluster. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil miẓuŋku and Malayalam miẓuŋŋuka independently give m-i-apical-u; Konda miṛiŋ supplies an independent high-i second-vowel variant. K03 p.161 explicitly uses *miẓ-u-ŋ.

**Direction.** Full southern and Konda forms establish m-V-apical order. Telugu mriŋgu is innovative, and its miŋgu variant can be traced through r loss because the cluster is independently attested in Telugu.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *miẓ-u-ŋk > *miẓ-ŋk > *mẓiŋk > mriŋgu > miŋgu, with nasal-stop voicing and postconsonantal ẓ>r. Konda miṛiŋ > *mṛiŋ > ṛiŋ gives first-member loss under the displacement account. Tamil/Malayalam v-initial forms need a separate labial history.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not replace all historical V2 values with u: the Konda i form is real and may involve assimilation. Kannada/Kota/central miŋ(g) can result directly from medial ẓ loss, or contact with Telugu, so matching modern Telugu miŋgu is not independent proof of concealed metathesis. Pengo ṛuggiŋga/ṛugginda is explicitly onomatopoeic and has different vowels/formation. Tamil English gloss words consume/devour are parser errors, not linguistic witnesses.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 pp.161–162; K61 pp.61–64; DEDR 4866

<a id="d4876"></a>
## d4876: shine, flash, lightning; star

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4876 |
| Comparative input | *min / *min-uŋ/ukk; long star *mīn; regional *min-s |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/ī / short verbal root and independent long star formation |
| C2 identity / structure | n / nasal; regional r/ḍ secondary |
| Following vowel | u/zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-C / CVC-u-CC; long noun |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Independent short/long lexical formations and Kuvi retained miṇs; exact long verbal grade unresolved. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for nasal root; medium for immediate long verb |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | late-kuvi-nasal-mixed-formation |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil miṉ/miṉuŋku, Malayalam minnuka and Kannada minugu establish a nasal root and short/long formation contrast independently. Kuvi miṇs, miṇig and mirsi coexist with mṇih/mṇīh and supply especially close regional input evidence.

**Direction.** The full nasal root across southern languages and retained Kuvi miṇs favor pre-vowel nasal promotion for mṇih. Gondi/Konda r/ḍ variants show that the apical may change identity before or after reordering; their existence does not prove all Kuvi nasals are secondary.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Regional miṇ-s > mṇi-s with h~st stem alternation can yield mṇih (mṇist-). The Isr. long mṇīh requires separate length or earlier vowel-coalescence history, not automatically the long star root. Telugu minuku:minku shows medial syncope retaining m-i-n order; miḍũgu versus miṇũgu involves nasal/stop change without metathesis. North bīnko/bínḍke has initial m>b and suffixal/cluster developments, not nasal promotion.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep short shine and long star formations separate. The fish reconstruction linked in this entry should not replace shine-root quantity; possible common origin with4885 is sensitivity only. Kuvi mrih has rhotic rather than nasal, and full mirsi could precede it by the ordinary nonnasal process; the exact order of n>r and reordering is not independently dated. mṇispu spelling lightening is the source gloss, not a different weather concept. Tulu broken HTML fragments miṇ&lt/kuni/&gt are not independent lexical forms.

**Mechanism scope.** Short nasal reordering supported; long variant and n/r chronology unresolved.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR4876 p.435 directly read; PSS83 p.232 n.5

<a id="d4885"></a>
## d4885: fish

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4885 |
| Comparative input | *mīn; Kuvi mīn-ka |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | ī / long independently attested; Pengo/Manda short |
| C2 identity / structure | n / nasal |
| Following vowel | zero/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC + plural-k(a) |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Attested singular stem plus plural -ka; source/dialect plural alternatives. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | late-kuvi-long-nasal-plural |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil mīṉ, Malayalam/Kannada mīn, Telugu mīnu and the Gondi/Konda/Kui forms independently establish long vowel before nasal. Kuvi singular mīnu and retained S. plural mīnka establish the immediate morphological input without relying on a reconstruction.

**Direction.** The full singular and alternative plural mīnka make m-n-ī in mnīka innovative. F. mrīka has secondary rhotic in the displaced cluster, not an independently primary r root.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** mīn-u + -ka > mīn-ka > mnī-ka, with dialectal mṇīka and mrīka requiring place/rhotic developments. Isr. singular mṇīnu retains the old postvocalic n as well as cluster ṇ: it is plausibly remodeled from the plural, or has nasal excrescence, rather than a literal one-for-one exchange. Kui mīnu:mīnga and Konda mīn:mīnga retain order.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The singular cluster variant must not count as independent confirmation of a swap because it contains two nasals. Distinguishing analogical backformation from phonetic excrescence needs chronology and paradigms across speakers. Fish4885 and shine/star4876 may be historically related through bright/scaly semantics, but this is not established; merge only in a sensitivity partition. DEDR main parser omits Gadaba/Gondi/Konda and strands Isr. forms in glosses; source-restored observations preserve the complete printed paradigms. Sanskrit mīna is a contact comparison, not a Dravidian language denominator.

**Mechanism scope.** Direct long vowel–nasal plural reordering; secondary cluster place change and possible singular analogy.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR4885 p.436 directly read; PSS83 p.232 n.5; Hume2004 p.225

## d4968: hare

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4968 |
| Comparative input | *muc/y-al; regional *mol/mor-Vl, K80 *moẓ-al |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | u/o / short |
| C2 identity / structure | secondary l/r, earlier c/y / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/o |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-l |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Two-liquid regional formation descends from a palatal/glide root; stages must precede a narrow-apical classification. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for broad order; medium for secondary-apical intermediate |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | secondary-apical-regional |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil mucal/muyal and Malayalam muyal independently support a low-a final-l formation with medial c/y. Gondi molol/malol and Konda morol establish a regional two-liquid stage before initial clusters. K80 *moẓ-al is a scholarly intermediate, not a directly attested Proto-Dravidian root.

**Direction.** Full southern and Gondi/Konda forms favor m-V-C-V-l before Kui mṛāḍu and Kuvi mrālu. Regional apical identity is clearer than its exact relation to the southern palatal/glide.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Regional *mor-al/ol > *mrōl > mrālu gives Kui/Kuvi with lowering and Kui final l>ḍ; Pengo mrōl retains the mid vowel. The deeper *mucal > moyal > regional molol/morol requires palatal weakening plus assimilation/rhotacism, whose order relative to metathesis is not directly dated. Central/northern nasal forms reflect other c/nc developments.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** No Telugu attestation in this group. The independently low-a southern ending supports a historical formation, but reconstructing first-syllable o rather than u needs the umlaut/relative chronology argument. Do not classify this as ordinary inherited PDr apical metathesis without the secondary-apical stages. K80 p.498 additionally quotes Indi mnāl/mnōl, absent from this group; later nasal clusters need separate source annotation.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 p.498 item15; DEDR 4968; K03 *muc-Vl/*moy-al

## d4971: rough, knotty; tree stump

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil muraṭu, Malayalam muraṭu and Kannada moraḍu independently establish a full low-a dental formation; Telugu moraḍu retains the same order.

**Direction.** Full agreement favors Telugu mrōḍu innovation; Kui mrōjo independently has cluster order in the tree-base meaning.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *mor-aḍ > mrōḍ by displacement/coalescence. Kui mrōjo adds dental-palatal correspondence. Nasal moṇḍi can reflect a separate assimilated derivative and is not proof of a previous mr stage.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Exact full/cluster Telugu pair supports direction and quantity, but coexistence requires lexical/formation history: the stump submeaning changes while broader rough derivatives retain r medially. Do not define a phonological class by that outcome. Gravel words have Indo-Aryan comparisons and need separate transmission study.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 4971; current comparative cluster panel

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil muri/murukku/muruŋku and central murk independently establish full short-vowel order; Malayalam mūruka is a long grade, not evidence all inputs were long.

**Direction.** Full comparisons favor eastern mr and Telugu br innovations; m>b is separate from displacement.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *mur-k > mruk, then Kui mruk-p > mrupk in the separate suffixal process. Telugu *mur-ŋg > *mruŋg > bruŋgu; *mur-y > bruyyu involves labial denasalization/strengthening. Full muruŋku leaves syncope versus later shortening open.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Death/kill derivatives and ordinary breaking forms coexist. Do not count bruŋgu sink4993 as an independent reflex of this r root: it has a competing semantic history and different apical. Long mrūva versus short mrunga in Kui needs formation-level quantity analysis.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 4975; current comparative cluster panel

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil muraṟci and Tulu murajɛ independently supply a low-a formative; Gondi moros/moras/maronj gives matching regional rhotic and final s/nj formations. First-vowel u/o/a variation remains important.

**Direction.** Tamil/Tulu/Gondi establish m-V-r before Kui mrāsu. Kuvi database marcu preserves m-a-r, while K80 prints a long-vowel form in the same comparison.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Regional *mor-a-s > *mrōs > mrās gives Kui under K80 lowering. K80’s deeper *mut-a/*mot-a > *mor-a requires a separate t/r correspondence argument. Kuvi marcu may retain order; the long form cited by K80 may reflect a different quantity grade or metathesis followed by vowel reinsertion, neither demonstrated.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Kui direction is plausible with strong suffix support, but not all branches share the same material or rope construction. The Kui leather rope versus Gondi tree fibre could reflect semantic specialization or contact. Telugu is unattested here. Preserve discrepancy between short database Kuvi marcu and long K80 spelling instead of silently normalizing it or counting two independent roots.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 p.498 item16; DEDR 4976

**Independent input evidence.** Telugu mola, Konda mola and Gondi molkī establish medial l; Kolami/Naikri mulke and Parji mulka preserve the cluster needed for the Brahui comparison.

**Direction.** Full regional l and lk support loss of cluster-initial l in Brahui mux, without requiring initial ml-.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *mul-k > *muk > mux by lateral loss and velar frication is Emeneau 1997 p.441 §2.2. Regional o/u and Telugu malugu/malumu require vowel/derivational histories independent of metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Brahui mux is an opaque other development, not a retained-apical negative and not evidence for hidden metathesis. **Mechanism scope.** Medial l loss before k; no independent evidence of initial metathesis.

<a id="d4993"></a>
## d4993: sink, immerse, drown

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d4993 |
| Comparative input | *muẓ-u-nk / *muẓ-u-nkk; long and shorter formations |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | u / mixed by formation |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/i/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u-NK / CVVC-K / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Independent high-u nasal-velar formation; long roots and different voice suffixes remain distinct. |
| Input class | mixed-or-uncertain-quantity |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil muẓuku, Malayalam muẓukuka, Kannada muẓuŋgu and Gondi muṛuŋg independently establish m-u-apical-u. Tulu murk and Konda muṛg/muṛk support a medial consonant-cluster branch.

**Direction.** Full SD I and Gondi/Konda forms establish earlier m-V-apical; Telugu bruŋgu has a moved apical and an additional initial m>b change. Full muḍũgu remains in Telugu itself.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *muẓ-u-ŋk > *muẓ-ŋk > *mẓuŋk > *mruŋg > bruŋgu; the initial denasalization m>b is separate (K61 p.28 §1.69). Alternatively vowel contraction and later shortening before NK can give the same short output. Bruncu has a different stronger transitive formation. Telugu muṇugu/munũgu and southern muŋg/mukk can arise by medial assimilation without initial metathesis.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This is another independent same-u short outcome, contradicting obligatory surface ū but not uniquely deciding syncope versus contraction plus shortening. Kui bṛuḍga adds a retroflex stop whose origin cannot be read off the Telugu ŋg; Kuvi mrūkʰali differs in quantity and suffix/aspiration. The shared initial b in Telugu and Kui is suggestive but insufficient to choose inheritance, independent denasalization or contact. None of the surviving mu-initial assimilated forms can be labeled hidden metathesis without separate evidence.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K61 p.28 §1.69, pp.61–64; K03 *muẓ-u-nk/nkk; DEDR 4993

## d5007: spoil, become mouldy; dirt

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5007 |
| Comparative input | *muṟ-i; *muṟ-k/g |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | u / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core-formation-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil muṟi, Telugu muṟiki/muṟugu, Gondi murk and Tulu murguni independently support full apical order and consonantal variants.

**Direction.** Full and cluster comparanda favor Telugu mrukku innovation; r-less muggu has a direct internal assimilation alternative.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *muṟ-k > mrukk with reordering/strengthening; *muṟ-ik > *muṟk by syncope is possible. mrukku > mukku is supported by the pair, while muggu could arise directly as in Kannada muggu.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Distinguish same-surface ripen mruggu5017/5046 from mouldy mrukku. Dirt and putrefaction meanings fit one family, but cannot fix vowel deletion chronology. Long mūri stench is a separate grade.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5007; current comparative cluster panel

## d5017: ripen, mature

| Property | Annotation |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam muṟṟu independently establish a strong apical root; Tamil muṟuku adds a velar variant, but its exact historical segmentation is uncertain.

**Direction.** Te mruggu might reflect a weakened/suffixed apical variant or5046; the source explicitly gives both options.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *muṟ-kk > mrugg requires a singleton apical plus velar suffix independently distinguished from *muṟṟ-u; *mūẓ-k > mrugg additionally requires shortening. Neither is securely selected.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep A, not a counterexample rescued by postulating degemination. Southern strong-root retention is an informative control. Historical full Telugu variant or cognate suffix paradigm would separate the analyses.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5017; current comparative cluster panel

## d5078: soft, weak, gentle; knead

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5078 |
| Comparative input | *mel; *mel-k; strong *mell- |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | l / singleton and geminate and l-k cluster |
| Following vowel | i/u/a / zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-V / CVC-k / CVCC |
| Grammatical category | adjective/verb/adverb |
| Boundary evidence | plausible formative boundary; not independently dated |

| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for mel-k order; conditional for Kui exact formative |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | cluster-loss-control |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil mel/meli/melku, Malayalam mel/meliyuka, Kannada mel/melu/melpu and Kota melg:melk independently support e-l and a velar formation.

**Direction.** Brahui bēɣ- can be derived directly from medial mel-k; Kui mṛērna has a cluster absent from the full comparanda but its exact formative is uncertain.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Emeneau 1997 p.442 §4 derives *mel-k > *bel-k > bēɣ with front-vowel-conditioned m>b, e>ē and cluster lateral loss. The exact order of lengthening and loss is not proved. Kui *mel-V-r/n > *mlV-r/n > mṛērna is a possible displacement comparison, with suffix and long ē still underdetermined.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The database reconstruction *mēl high/west is a wrong homonymous association, excluded. Strong mell- adverbs are not independent root votes. Brahui ē is not proof of a long proto-root: Emeneau treats it as the reflex of earlier short e under a contact-affected vowel inventory. Gadaba mellaga may be a Telugu loan; source checking is needed.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR5078; Emeneau1997 pp.441–442 §§2.1–4

## d5082: smear, plaster, wax

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5082 |
| Comparative input | *meẓ-u-k; other *meẓ-V-nḍ/ŋk/w formations |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | e/i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u / unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-u-K / CVC-V-NK / CVC-V-w |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | High-u velar, high-i palatal and uncertain low-a nasal/labial formations separate. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for apical order; low for proposed exact low-a input |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | vowel-input-uncertain |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil meẓuku, Malayalam meẓukuka and Konda miṛis independently establish an apical root and high-vowel formations. No compared form independently supplies the exact low-a formative required by K80 *meẓ-a for the Telugu/Kui long outputs.

**Direction.** Southern and Konda/Brahui full forms favor m-V-apical before Telugu mrē- and Kui mrānḍa. Thus order is firmer than exact quantity/formative conditioning.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *meẓ-a-ŋk > *mẓēŋk > mrē̃gu > mē̃gu gives Telugu if low a is justified; *meẓ-a-nḍ > *mẓēnḍ > mrānḍa adds Kui lowering. High-u/zero inputs could instead involve other contraction/lengthening routes. Telugu mrēvu has a different final labial development, not a free substitute for ŋg. Kuvi mrispi matches the high-i Konda form more closely.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A real quantity/formative residual: do not use long ē/ā to manufacture the a whose prediction is being tested. Telugu mēdu could be another formation or internal assimilation and is uncertain. Kolami mēg/Naikri mēgh may be old Telugu loans or independently medially reduced forms. Kuvi mṇek introduces a nasal not directly expected from ẓ, so its cognacy/assimilation needs separate evidence.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K80 p.498 item17; DEDR 5082; PSS83 parenthesized a reconstruction discussed in prior source audit

## d5124: ladle, draw water by dipping

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5124 |
| Comparative input | *moḷ-k / *muḷ-k |
| Initial consonant | m |
| V1 quality / quantity | o/u / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ḷ / lateral plus velar formative |
| Following vowel | zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb |

| Input confidence | high for earlier order; medium for root vowel and common inheritance |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core-cluster-secondary-nasal |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil moḷ and Malto mulɣe independently establish vowel-before-lateral order across southern and northern branches. Malto also supports a velar extension independently of the eastern clusters.

**Direction.** The two separated full comparisons favor *mVḷ-k before eastern ml/mr/mṇ forms. A deeper nasal root is not independently supported by these witnesses.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *mo/uḷ-k > *mḷo/uk > Kui mluk, Pengo/Manda mṛuk; Kuvi mṇok adds lateral-to-nasal assimilation before or after cluster formation. Kuvi mrokʰ-nai retains a rhotic alternative. Root o/u and the gloss merge in Schulze need separate scrutiny.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** This case cannot be counted as independent evidence that inherited nasals entered the original Telugu rule: the comparative input is lateral. Whether Kuvi assimilated a liquid after promotion or had a preexisting nasal allomorph is unresolved. DEDR3790 noḷ is an explicitly suggested comparison; initial m/n variation and semantics require review before merging families.

**Mechanism scope.** Consonantal apical displacement-family plus secondary nasal assimilation in Kuvi.

**Scholarly references.** DEDR5124, DED(S)4209; comparison3790 not merged

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible older *mVr-a > *mrā followed by rhotic/nasal variation is only a schematic hypothesis. Alternatively the cluster may be inherited at the immediate common stage. Pengo mṛā-kʰa thief and mouse compounds suggest agentive morphology followed by a rodent noun, not extra root changes.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Leave the earlier input and presence of historical reordering unresolved. Needed: an independently cognate full root, regular r/n correspondences and the semantics of the mouse compound. Do not infer borrowing simply to avoid the missing input, or use the already clustered proto-head as evidence of a Telugu-like change.

## d5153: year; this/last/next year compounds

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5153 |
| Comparative input | *yĀṇṭ-u; K80 *nīt-yāṇṭ > *nir-ēṇḍ/*nir-ōṇḍ |
| Initial consonant | y/zero; compound n |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā/ē/ō; compound i / long bare root; compound first-member quantity unresolved |
| C2 identity / structure | ṇṭ; compound r / singleton |
| Following vowel | compound boundary |
| Root/formation shape | (C)VVNC / CVC#VVNC |
| Grammatical category | noun/adverb |
| Boundary evidence | Completed + year and deictic + year must be independently segmented; bare year supplies no initial rhotic. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high for year; low for exact completed-year compound stages |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | compound-process-separate |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil yāṇṭu/āṇṭu, Kodagu āṇḍɨ and Telugu ēṇḍu independently establish the long year root. Last-year r-initial forms contain additional material; the year root itself has no r that could be simply transposed to its beginning.

**Direction.** K80 p.498 item18 proposes completed+year *nīt-yāṇṭ with regional nir-ēṇḍ/nir-ōṇḍ and quotes Konda nṛund. This supports a compound-based comparison, but the exact full compound and shortening are not independently attested in the present group.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Bare *yĀṇṭ > āṇṭ/ēṇḍ/ōnḍ retains order after glide/vowel changes. Conditional *nir#ōṇḍ > *nrōṇḍ > ṛōnḍ and lowered ṛānḍ gives the last-year forms; merger, shortening and resegmentation at the compound boundary must be separately justified. Pengo/Manda ṛāṭihiŋ has further suffix and nasal-loss history.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not count last-year as ordinary metathesis of the bare year root or use its morphology-free head to test a vowel rule. Kui ṛānḍu last year versus ṛōnḍu previous year preserve a meaning distinction, potentially analogical rather than free phonetic variation. K80 prints Kui twice where the second set appears to be Kuvi; DEDR independently confirms Kuvi r-initial forms. Corpus-wide Konda gloss search last year returned zero; K80 nṛund is a source-only observation. Complete-root component remains to be independently linked.

**Mechanism scope.** Bare root retention; proposed compound metathesis requires separate denominator.

**Scholarly references.** K80 p.498 item18 directly visually checked; DEDR 5153

<a id="d5159"></a>
## d5159: river, water, thirst

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5159 |
| Comparative input | *yĀṯ-u, oblique *yĀṯṯ-; regional *ēṯ |
| Initial consonant | y/zero |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā/ē / long |
| C2 identity / structure | ṟ/ṯ / singleton |
| Following vowel | u/zero |
| Root/formation shape | (C)VVC / (C)VVCC |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Free water root versus oblique/number and big-river compounds; compound first member excluded from root screen. |
| Input class | long-apical-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil yāṟu/āṟu with oblique ṟṟ, Malayalam āṟu, Telugu ēṟu/ēṭi and Gondi yēr/yēt independently establish long quantity and an apical paradigm. The difference ā/ē is linked to the special initial-y vowel correspondence, not to metathesis.

**Direction.** Long vowel precedes the apical across branches. Loss of initial y in southern forms does not move the apical, and eastern j/y/z/s reflexes remain after the vowel.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *yĀṯu > āṟu/ēṟu retains order after initial glide loss and regional vowel developments. Oblique fortition gives Tamil āṟṟu and Telugu ēṭi. Kui ēju/ēsu and Pengo ēz/ēs show apical changes without initial displacement.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** A strong long-vowel control across Telugu and eastern languages. Tulu tārɯ/sārɯ/hārɯ add or preserve initial material requiring separate local explanation, but final r stays postvocalic. Gondi and central big-river compounds combine this root with per/bere big; do not screen that compound-initial per as the river input. Badaga proper names are not independent basic reflexes. Imported goat reconstruction is erroneous metadata.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5159; K03 initial *yĀ and apical-oblique correspondence

## d5250: stream, river, pit

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5250 |
| Comparative input | regional *vant; extra-r variant |
| Initial consonant | v |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | nt / nasal-stop |
| Following vowel | zero/i |
| Root/formation shape | CVNC |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | nasal-or-nasal-cluster-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | secondary-r-input-unresolved |

**Independent input evidence.** Kolami/Naikri vanta and Telugu vanta independently supply a nasal-stop root without r.

**Direction.** Telugu vranti adds r while retaining nt; this is not a simple permutation of the compared input.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible secondary r, contamination by a flow/channel root such as the source cross-references5296/5356, or an older two-apical compound; none is established.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep A for cluster. Need older full r-bearing form and source contexts for river versus pit. A word-initial cluster alone does not justify *var-anti.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5250; current comparative cluster panel

<a id="d5263"></a>
## d5263: write, draw lines, scratch

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5263 |
| Comparative input | *war-ay; *war-i and other scratching formations |
| Initial consonant | w |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a/i |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-ay / CVC-i |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Low-ay write versus high-i scratch/test formations independently attested; derivatives and recipient writing vocabulary not independent roots. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil varai and Malayalam varayuka independently establish low-a drawing formation; Kannada bare and Tulu barepini corroborate labial-V-r order. Tamil vari independently establishes a high-i counterpart.

**Direction.** Multiple southern forms support var- before Telugu vrā-. The coexistence of vrāyu/rāyu directly supports subsequent loss of the first cluster member, unlike Telugu finger vrēlu>vēlu.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *war-ay > *wrāy > vrāyu > rāyu. Writing nouns vrā̃ta/vrālu and causative vrāyincu have distinct suffix histories. Telugu variyu metal-testing preserves the high-i formation. Kui vrīsa/Kuvi brīnai has high ī and different suffix history, potentially *war-i versus a different earlier vowel grade.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** One first-member-loss word does not establish a universal low-vowel rule for wr clusters. Literacy vocabulary readily diffuses: Gondi/Konda/Kuvi rās/rāc and Gadaba rāyap may be Telugu exports or reflect local developments. Gondi varasānā retains full order, but its relation to a possible borrowed rās is uncertain. Telugu baruku and Parji varc have explicit alternative d5322 etymologies. Badaga finger/place-name homonyms attached to this group are not writing reflexes.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K61 pp.67–68; K03 pp.157–158; PSS83 pp.230–231; DEDR 5263

<a id="d5295"></a>
## d5295: scrape, wipe, erase inscription

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5295 |
| Comparative input | *waẓ-i; *waẓ-C / *waẓ-a/icu causative formations |
| Initial consonant | w |
| V1 quality / quantity | a / short |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/a/zero |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i / CVC-C |
| Grammatical category | verb |
| Boundary evidence | Exact short -cc formation is not independently identical to Kannada low-a -acu; preserve this unresolved step. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | medium |
| Overall confidence | high for order; medium for full formation |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil vaẓi and Kannada baẓi/baẓicu/baẓacu establish w/b-V-ẓ and different vowel-bearing extensions. Telugu vẓaccu preserves the identity of the promoted approximant before its merger with r.

**Direction.** Independent southern medial ẓ plus old Telugu cluster vẓ supports displacement before postconsonantal ẓ>r. The surviving cluster consonant is stronger direction evidence than a modern r alone.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** A consonantal *waẓ-cc > *wẓacc > vraccu accounts for short a with cc; alternatively high-i syncope could precede the consonantal stage. Kannada baẓacu has low a and cannot be mechanically chosen as the exact immediate Telugu input without explaining the short output. Telugu baḍiyu retains V before the apical in a different ritual sweeping formation.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The exact causative/input vowel remains a substantive uncertainty; old cluster spelling does not solve it. Inscriptional vẓ/vr dates need separate localization. Badaga bāku may have medial assimilation/loss and lengthening rather than initial metathesis. Toda poṛt ud contains the comparison in a compound; bare ud must not be counted as another independent reflex of waẓ.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5295; K61 pp.67–68; K03 p.158 apical reflex table

## d5372: live, flourish, livelihood

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5372 |
| Comparative input | *wāẓ; short *waẓ-d-uk / regional *bar-d-uk |
| Initial consonant | v/b |
| V1 quality / quantity | ā/a / long root and independently short derivative |
| C2 identity / structure | ẓ/r / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/u |
| Root/formation shape | CVVC / CVC-C-V-C |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |

| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil vāẓ and Kannada bāẓ establish long root; Kannada barduku/barduŋku and baẓduŋku independently support a short expanded apical-dental formation.

**Direction.** Kannada barduku favors Telugu braduku reordering without projecting the long bare-root vowel onto this derivative. Possible early regional borrowing would still permit local displacement.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** *bar-d-uk > bra-d-uk, with initial w>b and apical development preceding or independent of the observed order change; bratuku has dental voicing variation. baduku/batuku can be direct apical loss or later cluster loss.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The apical is followed by d and a further u-k suffix: morphology is crucial. The apparent Telugu b&lt, br&lt and &gt are transcription/editorial fragments, not forms. Neither Arabic barkat cross-reference nor unrelated Badaga place names establish cognacy.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5372; current comparative cluster panel

<a id="d5409"></a>
## d5409: finger

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5409 |
| Comparative input | *wir/wer-al; distinct *wir-and/anj derivatives |
| Initial consonant | w |
| V1 quality / quantity | i/e / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-a-L / CVC-a-NC |
| Grammatical category | noun |
| Boundary evidence | Southern -al and regional -and/-anj are independently different formations; no free substitution of suffix consonants. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high |
| Overall confidence | high |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil/Malayalam viral, Kannada beral/beraḷ and Tulu berel independently establish initial labial, V, rhotic, then a second vowel/liquid. Gondi varanj/virinj and regional *-and/anj forms are different formations. K03 pp.101–106 explains historical i/e ambiguity.

**Direction.** The full southern forms and retained Gondi/Konda variants support labial–vowel–rhotic order. Telugu vrēlu reverses the relative vowel/rhotic order, and vēlu is its documented cluster-reduced counterpart.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Immediate *wer-al > *wrēl > vrēlu > vēlu. Deeper *wir-al > *wer-al lowering is one analysis; ancestral e is an alternative where southern vowel mergers obscure the contrast. Simple initial-vowel deletion from weral would give wral with wrong quality; prior a>e assimilation plus deletion gives wrēl without literal exchange.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** The exact mechanism remains underdetermined but plain deletion alone is inadequate. Konda veṛska versus ṛeska/ṛaska permits *vṛ- > ṛ- with first-member loss; exact a/e suffix history differs from Telugu -al. Kui vanju/Kuvi vansu and Central vande admit medial r assimilation in a nasal-stop formation; they are not secure concealed initial metathesis. Toda pēḷ can likewise arise by medial r loss and contraction. Badaga bēru index finger has a competing relation to full beralu or another finger-name root.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** K03 pp.101–106,483; K61 pp.61–62,67; PSS83 ch.15; DEDR 5409

<a id="d5411"></a>
## d5411: open, split, go to pieces

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5411 |
| Comparative input | *wir-i; *wir-i-nk/nkk; proposed *wir-il |
| Initial consonant | w |
| V1 quality / quantity | i / short |
| C2 identity / structure | r / singleton |
| Following vowel | i/u/a |
| Root/formation shape | CVC-i / CVC-i-NK / CVC-i-l? |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | High-vowel root independently attested; lateral derivative remains a hypothesis and cannot verify its own prediction. |
| Input class | short-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant |
| Telugu hypothesis | eligible; obligatory application predicts D |
| Input confidence | high for root; low for exact Telugu -il suffix |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | core |

**Independent input evidence.** Tamil viri, Malayalam viriyuka, Kannada biri and Konda viris/virs independently establish w-i-r and high-vowel formations. The extra lateral in Telugu vrīlu requires a derivative, and K61 explicitly says the proposed -il/-ul is unattested elsewhere.

**Direction.** Many branches agree on w-V-r before Telugu/Kui/Kuvi vr-. Telugu virugu/viriyu retains order alongside vrīlu. An earlier *vir-il is a published immediate antecedent, not an independently verified Proto-Dravidian word.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Conditional *wir-il > *wrīl > vrīlu gives the long displaced Telugu form if the suffix is established. *wir-i-nk > *wriŋk gives Kui vringa, while labial vrīva has its own quantity/formative history. Gondi rīk can follow *wrīk with w loss; source suffix comparison remains needed. Telugu viccu/vippu/vikku permits direct medial assimilation, independently paralleled by Kannada biccu and Tulu biccuni.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Do not claim deterministic output conditioning from a suffix reconstructed only to yield ī. The broader displacement interpretation is stronger than the exact vowel/derivative chronology. Gondi rīk could involve regional borrowing or a distinct velar derivative; retain medium confidence. Kui birasakali is unshifted-looking but expressive/deverbal formation may differ. Sanskrit aravinda comparison concerns a compound and adds no independent root vote.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5411; K61 p.67 §1.156 explicitly unattested derivative (prior verified reading); DEN1 1972 p.415 entry4438

<a id="d5555"></a>
## d5555: throw, strike, discharge

| Property | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| Primary family | d5555 |
| Comparative input | *wey; long grade and extra-r variants |
| Initial consonant | v |
| V1 quality / quantity | e/ē / short and long grades |
| C2 identity / structure | y / singleton |
| Following vowel | zero/unknown |
| Root/formation shape | CVC / CVVC |
| Grammatical category | verb/noun |
| Boundary evidence | Exact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output. |
| Input class | nonapical-or-uncertain-input |
| Telugu hypothesis | outside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule |
| Input confidence | Comparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes |
| Overall confidence | medium |
| Eligibility / caveat | secondary-r-input-unresolved |

**Independent input evidence.** Konda vey and Kuvi ve/vēp independently supply a nonrhotic root. Telugu vēyu/vaicu likewise has no medial r.

**Direction.** Te vrēyu/vrēṭu adds r absent from the comparative input; neither the glide nor dental can simply exchange with a vowel to supply it.

**Derivation and relative chronology.** Possible analogical r in vēyu>vrēyu followed by derivative spread, or older fuller root/compound not yet identified. Labial/dental suffix alternations in eastern forms do not independently establish r.

**Exceptions and discriminating evidence.** Keep A, including vrēṭu strike noun and compound. Need early full rhotic witness or a demonstrable analogical model. Modern Telugu r-less variants cannot alone establish r loss as the first history.

**Mechanism scope.** Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

**Scholarly references.** DEDR 5555; current comparative cluster panel
